question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: So, I was finally getting the hang of parallel parking, and I thought I had it.  I pulled up next to the curb, turned the wheel, and... the car just wouldn't budge.  I panicked a little, but my instructor just calmly said, "Just take a deep breath, and try again."  Turns out, I was too close to the curb and hadn't adjusted the steering wheel enough.  I'm still a little shaky about parallel parking, but I'm getting there!

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, trying to sound convincing.  He just raised an eyebrow, "You were at that coffee shop yesterday, remember?"  I sighed, "Yeah, but that was just a quick stop.  I'm going to the club, I promise."  He just shook his head and chuckled.  I guess he didn't believe me.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I was so frustrated. We'd been arguing for ages about how he doesn't seem to care about my feelings anymore.  It felt like he just didn't listen, and I was starting to feel unheard and unimportant.  I needed him to understand how much this hurt me, but I wasn't sure if he even wanted to.  It was a really tough conversation, and I'm still not sure if we're on the same page.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: My boyfriend said something the other day that really stung. He said my expectations of him are too high, and that I'm always looking for perfection.  I felt a little hurt, like he didn't understand how much I care about him and how much I want him to be the best he can be.  I guess I just need to talk to him about it, and maybe we can find a better way to communicate.  It's important to me that we're both happy and fulfilled in the relationship.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: My heart started pounding as the teacher's voice echoed through the room.  I felt my cheeks flush, and I wished I could disappear.  Everyone else seemed so animated, but I just sat there, lost in my thoughts.  It was embarrassing, but I knew I needed to work on being more confident in class.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: My phone buzzed with a text from Sarah, saying she was staying the night with her boyfriend.  I felt a little pang of disappointment, but also a sense of relief.  It was nice to have some space to myself, and I was looking forward to a quiet evening.  I made myself a cup of tea and settled in for a good book, feeling content with the quiet night.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I was really looking forward to that weekend trip, planning it for months.  Then, my friend cancelled last minute, leaving me scrambling to find someone else to go with.  It was frustrating, and I felt disappointed that I had to rearrange everything.  I guess sometimes people just don't think about how their actions affect others.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I was really swamped with my own deadlines, and I was already feeling the pressure.  He asked me to help with something that he could have easily done himself, and I felt frustrated.  It was a bit of a blow to my already tight schedule, and I just wanted to get back to my own work.  I tried to explain that I was really busy, but he just seemed to be in a hurry.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the shock and anger I felt when I heard about what happened.  It's just so cruel and disrespectful to end a pregnancy in such a way, and to throw away the remains like that.  It's a complete disregard for human life and dignity.  I just hope the authorities can bring some justice to this situation.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was glued to the TV, trying to follow the latest episode of my favorite show, when my little brother barged in.  He was already digging into a plate of cookies, completely ignoring me and my concentration.  I sighed, knowing I'd have to deal with him later, but for now, I just had to keep my eyes on the screen.  It was a constant battle, trying to enjoy my own entertainment while he was busy being a little whirlwind.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even imagine what it must be like to go through something like that.  It's just awful that someone would do that to someone else, especially someone walking home alone.  I'm so sorry she had to go through that.  I hope she's okay.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was just trying to get some work done on my laptop when this guy plopped down beside me on the bus.  He didn't even bother to close his zipper, and I was mortified.  I felt so uncomfortable and violated, and I couldn't help but stare at him in disbelief.  I just wanted to get off the bus as quickly as possible and get away from that awkward situation.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: Ugh, I swear my roommate is a human earthquake!  Every night, she's shaking the bed like it's a trampoline.  It's impossible to get any sleep with that going on, and I'm starting to think she's doing it on purpose.  I just want a peaceful night's rest, you know?

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get a nap on the bus when I saw a couple of guys acting shady.  They were trying to pickpocket people, and then suddenly, the whole bus erupted.  People were yelling and grabbing the guys, and then they were dragged out of the bus and beaten up pretty badly.  It was terrifying, and I felt so helpless just watching.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: I was trying to focus on my work, but this guy was playing this awful recorder, like a really bad, tinny version of a song.  It was just so distracting, and I didn't want to be rude, so I just kept trying to ignore it.  I ended up just getting up and heading to the coffee shop, hoping the noise wouldn't follow me.  It was a bit of a relief to get out of the room, honestly.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: I was just sitting here, reading a book, when I felt something crawling up my arm.  It was a tiny, little bug, and I couldn't help but freeze for a second.  I tried to swat it away, but it was too quick, and it just kept inching its way up my arm.  I ended up just letting it go, hoping it wouldn't bite.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I was buzzing from the game, but the moment I saw my friend behind the wheel, I knew something was off. He was speeding, weaving in and out of traffic, and his eyes were glazed over.  I tried to talk to him, but he just kept muttering about the "good times."  I felt sick to my stomach, knowing he was putting us all in danger.  I couldn't let him keep driving, so I finally had to tell him to pull over.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just enjoying the sunset in the garden, the air warm and still.  Then I saw it, a snake slithering slowly towards me, its scales glinting in the fading light.  My heart skipped a beat, and I froze, unsure of what to do.  I watched it for a moment, mesmerized by its sinuous movement, before it disappeared into the bushes.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up with a jolt, heart pounding, in the middle of the night.  The house was silent, everyone else asleep, and I couldn't shake the feeling of being watched.  I lay there for a moment, listening to the quiet hum of the house, before finally drifting back to sleep.  It was a strange feeling, being alone in the dark, but I knew it was just a random night.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: The front door clicked shut behind me, and I was alone.  My parents were gone, no note, no explanation, just an empty house.  The clock ticked past 6, and the silence was deafening.  I wandered around, trying to find something, anything, to explain the sudden emptiness.  It was getting late, and I was starting to feel scared.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I was just trying to get some attention from my friend, but I totally lost control and threw the duster.  It hit him right on the head, and I felt awful.  He was bleeding a little, and I knew the teacher would find out.  I just wanted to apologize and make it right, but I was so embarrassed.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just walking down the street, minding my own business, when two girls started yelling at me and making threats.  They kept coming at me, their voices getting louder and more aggressive.  I felt really scared and uncomfortable, and I just wanted to get away from them as quickly as possible.  It was a really unsettling experience, and I'm still shaken up about it.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already feeling stressed about merging onto the freeway, and then this truck started tailgating me like I was going to stop on a dime.  I was trying to keep my cool, but the car in front of me was doing the same thing, and I was practically on the edge of my seat.  Then, someone decided to change lanes without looking, and I swear I thought we were going to crash!  I just kept my foot on the gas and hoped for the best.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: I was so excited when the man in the red suit came to our house! He had a big sack and a twinkle in his eye, and he gave me a shiny new toy.  But then, this other guy in chains started making all these loud noises, like a grumpy monster.  It was kind of scary, but the man in the red suit just laughed and said it was just his helper, Sinterklaas.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: Ugh, I feel terrible. I completely spaced on calling my grandma for her birthday. I knew it was her day, but I just got caught up in everything else and totally forgot.  I feel awful that I let her down, especially since she always makes a big deal about her birthday.  I'm going to call her tomorrow and make it up to her.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I borrowed my friend's jacket for a weekend trip, and I was so excited to wear it.  I got back and realized there was a huge stain on the back, something I definitely didn't put there.  I felt awful, knowing I ruined it.  I'm hoping my friend will understand, but I'm already feeling bad about it.  I'll definitely be more careful in the future.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I was so stressed about the upcoming test, and I knew I hadn't finished my homework.  I panicked and told my teacher it was lost, hoping she wouldn't notice I hadn't even started.  But she caught on, and I felt awful.  I knew I had to own up to my mistake and try to make things right.  It was a big lesson about honesty and responsibility.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I felt awful when I realized I'd missed my feeding appointment for Mittens.  I'd been so busy with work and forgot all about it.  Now I'm scrambling to make it up to my neighbor, and hoping Mittens doesn't get too grumpy about it.  I'll definitely be more careful next time!

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I was so excited to finally get my new laptop for school, but I knew my parents had given me a specific amount for supplies.  I really wanted a cool backpack, so I ended up using some of the money for that instead.  I felt bad, but I figured it was a small sacrifice for something I really needed.  It was a good lesson about budgeting and making responsible choices.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I was so embarrassed when I realized I'd told a story about something someone confided in me to a few other people.  It felt like a betrayal, like I'd broken a trust.  I felt awful, especially since they were close friends of the person who originally told me.  I tried to apologize, but it felt like I couldn't make it up to them.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: Ugh, I feel terrible about it, but I had to cancel our plans last minute.  I just wasn't feeling up to going out, and I really wanted to stay home and relax.  I know it's not fair to my friend, but sometimes you just need a night in.  Hopefully, we can reschedule soon!

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I was just trying to make a quick cup of tea, and then BAM!  The glass shattered on the floor.  I immediately started looking around for the culprit, and my brother was the first one I saw.  He looked at me with a smirk, and I knew I was caught.  I just couldn't help but feel a little guilty, even though I knew I was the one who broke it.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I'll never forget the look on my sister's face when she finally held our son.  He was a big boy, bigger than anyone expected, and the delivery was rough.  The nurses were amazing, and my sister and I were both exhausted, but so relieved.  He was healthy and perfect, and that's all that mattered.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was sorting through some old boxes when I stumbled across a letter from Sarah, someone I hadn't seen in years.  It was from her college years, and she mentioned she was thinking about coming back to our hometown.  I was surprised, but also a little excited to hear from her again.  It felt like a little piece of the past had been rediscovered.  I can't wait to catch up with her when she gets back.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something wrong, like I'd said or done something to upset someone.  I was so worried about it, I even avoided them for a few days.  Then, I saw them smiling and laughing with someone else, and I realized I'd been overthinking things.  Turns out, they were just having a good time, and they actually liked me!

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it! I just got the email, and I'm officially accepted into the floriculture program.  It's been my dream since I was a kid, and now it's actually happening.  I'm so excited to learn all about flowers and how to make them beautiful.  This is going to be amazing!

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it! I just got accepted into the psychology program at my dream school.  I've been working towards this for so long, and now it's finally happening.  I'm so excited to dive into the world of human behavior and learn all I can.  This is a huge step in my life, and I'm ready to take on the challenge.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I was so surprised when I heard the radio announcement!  I couldn't believe it, I actually passed!  It feels amazing to know I'm going to secondary school, I'm really excited to learn more and explore new things.  I can't wait to see what the future holds.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My heart nearly stopped when I heard their voice, asking me out.  I'd admired them for years, their work and their personality always inspiring me.  It felt surreal, like a dream, but also incredibly exciting.  I managed to stammer out a yes, feeling a mix of nerves and pure joy.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My heart was pounding as the teacher praised my dancing.  She said I had a natural talent and could potentially join the ballet academy!  I was speechless, but I couldn't help but smile.  This was the best day ever, and I couldn't wait to see what the future held.  I knew I had a lot of work to do, but this was a huge step in the right direction.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It was weird, having my best friend gone for two whole years.  We used to do everything together, and suddenly it felt like a huge chunk of my life was missing.  But, I learned to appreciate the time I had with my other friends and found new hobbies to fill the void.  It was a tough adjustment, but I'm glad she's back now and we can pick up where we left off.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but the day my sister woke up from the coma was the day my life changed forever.  She was so weak, barely able to move or speak, and the doctors were constantly talking about the long road to recovery.  It was heartbreaking to see her like that, and the fear of what the future held was overwhelming.  But through it all, she's been fighting, and that's what keeps me going.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I was so disappointed when I found out I didn't get into the English college.  I poured my heart into my applications, and to be one percent short of the cutoff felt like a huge blow.  It's frustrating, especially when you've been dreaming of studying English for so long.  I guess I'll keep working hard and see what other opportunities come my way.  Maybe this is just a detour, not the end of the road.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: The thought of losing someone I love, someone I'd built a life with, was a heavy weight on my chest.  It felt like a mirror image of the pain I felt after losing my mentor, someone I looked up to and admired deeply.  The fear of losing another person I cherish was a constant shadow, a reminder of the fragility of life and the preciousness of our connections.  I knew I couldn't let that fear consume me, but it was a struggle to keep my heart from sinking.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I was really looking forward to catching up with some friends, but it felt awkward from the start.  They seemed distant and didn't really engage in the conversation.  It was clear they weren't thrilled to see me, and I felt a bit hurt and confused.  I guess sometimes people just aren't in the mood to socialize, and that's okay.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I was devastated when I found out someone had stolen all my friend's clothes from their cupboard.  It was a total mess, and they were so upset.  It was a huge blow to their confidence, and they were struggling to get ready for the day.  I felt awful for them, and we decided to go shopping for new clothes together.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe it. I poured my heart into studying for this exam, and now I'm not even on the list?  It feels like a punch to the gut, like all that hard work was for nothing.  I guess I just need to take a deep breath and figure out what comes next.  Maybe I can try again next year, or maybe I'll explore other options.  It's a bummer, but I'm not giving up on my dreams.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I was so disappointed when I saw my grade on the 8th-grade exam.  I'd been working hard all year, and to see it not reflect that felt awful.  It's a wake-up call to really focus on my studying and make sure I'm putting in the effort.  I know I can do better, and I'm determined to improve.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My heart was pounding like a drum solo as I raised my hand to answer the question.  I knew the answer, but my brain had decided to take a vacation and left me with a blank slate.  The whole class stared at me, and I could feel my face burning.  I mumbled a response, hoping it wouldn't be too obvious that I had no clue what I was talking about.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: I was so embarrassed when my friends found out I'd been talking badly about them.  It felt like a huge betrayal, and I was worried about how they'd feel.  I tried to apologize, but it felt like I couldn't make it up to them.  I really hope they can forgive me.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: My friend was telling this wild story, and I swear my brain just went blank.  I stared at them, trying to find the right words, but nothing came out.  I felt a little embarrassed, like I was failing at being a good listener.  I just mumbled something about how crazy it was, hoping they wouldn't notice my awkward silence.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe this happened! I was just walking to the park and I totally tripped on a loose rock and... well, let's just say I got a little bit of a surprise.  My shorts are ruined, and I'm pretty embarrassed.  I guess I'll have to go home and change.  This is the worst day ever.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I was trying to tell everyone how frustrated I was about the whole situation, but they just looked at me like I was crazy.  I felt like I was being judged for expressing myself, and it made me feel really uncomfortable.  I just wanted to be heard, but instead, I felt like I was being dismissed.  It was really disheartening.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: Ugh, I was so confident about that homework problem, I even brought in a solution I'd worked on.  But when I actually looked at the problem, I realized I had completely misread the instructions and my answer was completely off.  I felt so stupid, I just wanted to crawl under my desk.  I guess I need to pay more attention in class!

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a blast, dancing and feeling the music, when suddenly, the seam of my dress ripped open.  It was right in the middle, right above my knee, and I felt my cheeks flush red.  Everyone stopped dancing and stared, and I felt like I was going to faint.  I just stood there, mortified, trying to figure out how to fix it.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I swear, I was just trying to be sneaky, but I totally got caught.  My aunt's pantry is like a treasure trove, and I couldn't resist grabbing a few cookies.  I was so caught off guard when she caught me, and now I'm feeling pretty embarrassed.  I guess I'll just have to face the music and apologize.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: I slammed on the brakes, white-knuckled on the wheel, and the car lurched.  It was supposed to be a smooth, controlled stop, but I felt like I was going to throw up.  The instructor just stared at me, his face blank, and I wanted to scream.  This was supposed to be a learning experience, not a nightmare.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, my voice tight.  They just scoffed, "You were at that coffee shop yesterday, remember?"  I felt my blood boil.  How could they doubt me?  I'm not some phantom, I'm going to be out there, living my life.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I'm sick of it.  He just doesn't get it, doesn't see how I feel.  He acts like I'm overreacting, like I'm making a big deal out of nothing.  I'm tired of being ignored, tired of feeling like I'm invisible.  This isn't how a relationship should be.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: I felt like my stomach dropped.  He just said that?  Like I'm some kind of demanding, impossible creature to please?  It's like he doesn't even see me, just sees a checklist of things he's supposed to be doing.  I'm furious.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: I felt my cheeks burn as the teacher called on me, and then she pointed right at me, like I was some kind of freak show.  The whole class stared, and I wanted to disappear.  It was like she was mocking me, making me the center of attention for all the wrong reasons.  I just wanted to crawl under the desk and never come out.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: I slammed the phone down, the sound echoing through the empty house.  Her words, "I'll spend the night," felt like a punch to the gut.  Why couldn't she just be honest?  This constant need to be with him, to be close, it's like a festering wound.  I just want to be alone.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I just found out they lied to me.  It's like they completely disregarded everything we talked about.  I feel sick to my stomach, like I can't breathe.  It's just infuriating, and I don't know what to do.  I need to get out of here.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I was already swamped with my own deadlines, and he just had to come to me for a hand?  He knew he had more time than me to finish his part, so why did he even ask?  It's like he doesn't even respect my time or my workload.  Honestly, it's infuriating.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to process what I just learned.  It's like someone ripped a piece of my world out and threw it in a garbage can.  How could someone do that?  It's just...unfathomable.  I feel sick.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was finally getting into the show, the kind with the good music and the interesting plot, when my brother just barged in.  He started grabbing snacks from the counter, completely ignoring me.  It's like he doesn't even care that I'm trying to enjoy my evening.  I wanted to scream, but I just glared at him.  It's so frustrating when he acts like he owns the place.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even believe what happened.  She was just walking home, minding her own business, and this jerk just attacked her.  It's just so awful, and I can't imagine what she's going through.  I'm furious, and I just want to make sure she's okay.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was trying to get some peace and quiet on the bus, but this guy just had to ruin it.  He sat down next to me, and I swear I could feel my blood pressure rising.  His pants were open, and I couldn't look away.  It was like he was trying to make me uncomfortable, and I just wanted to scream.  I felt so violated, like I was being violated right there in the middle of the bus.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: I tried to ignore it, but the constant shaking and noise just wouldn't stop.  It felt like someone was trying to break my concentration, like they were deliberately trying to keep me awake.  I wanted to scream, to tell her to just be quiet, but I knew that wouldn't help.  It was like she didn't even care about the fact that I was trying to sleep.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get home, minding my own business, when I saw it.  Two guys, clearly up to no good, were being dragged off the bus by a mob of people.  They were beating the crap out of them, and I couldn't believe it.  It was like something out of a movie, but it was real.  I felt sick to my stomach, watching it all unfold.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: That blasted recorder was driving me crazy.  It was like nails on a chalkboard, just screeching and droning.  I tried to ignore it, but it was impossible.  I just needed to get out of here, find some peace and quiet.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I was just trying to relax, and this little bug decided to crawl up my arm.  It felt like it was crawling on my skin, and I just wanted to fling it off.  I swear, it was like it was mocking me.  I'm so over this.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: My stomach was churning, not from the beer I'd had, but from the way my friend was driving.  He was weaving in and out of traffic, ignoring the red lights, and I could feel my heart pounding in my chest.  I tried to keep my voice calm, but every time he sped up, I felt a surge of anger.  This wasn't just reckless, it was dangerous, and I was terrified.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just enjoying the peace of the garden, the air warm and still.  Then I saw it, slithering closer, its scales glinting in the fading light.  My heart hammered in my chest, a cold dread crawling up my spine.  I wanted to scream, to run, but my legs felt rooted to the spot.  It was a terrifying, primal fear, a feeling of being hunted.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: The silence was thick and suffocating, broken only by the rhythmic thump of my own heart.  I sat up, the cold floor biting into my bare skin, and the room felt like a tomb.  Why couldn't they just leave me alone?  Why couldn't they understand that I needed this space, this quiet, this time to breathe?

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see my family, but the house was empty.  No one was in the living room, no one was in the kitchen, not even a note.  The clock ticked by, each second an eternity, and the silence was deafening.  I was alone, and it felt like someone had ripped the air out of the room.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I just snapped.  It was like a fuse blew, and I couldn't stop myself.  I threw the duster, and it connected with that kid's head.  I felt a rush of satisfaction, but then the guilt hit me like a ton of bricks.  I knew I'd messed up, and I was terrified of what was coming.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to get a coffee, minding my own business, when these two girls just started yelling at me.  They were spitting insults and making threats, and I felt like I was trapped in a nightmare.  They wouldn't stop, and it was like they were trying to intimidate me into doing something I didn't want to do.  I just wanted to get away from them, but they wouldn't let me.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already sweating, the rain making the air thick and heavy.  Then this truck, like a metal monster, was right on my bumper, and the car in front of me was doing that stupid lane change thing.  I slammed on the brakes, my heart pounding, and felt like I was going to lose control.  It was a miracle I didn't end up in a ditch.  This whole commute was turning into a nightmare.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: That blasted bell kept ringing, like a giant was trying to wake me up from a dream.  The guy in the red suit was all smiles, but his companion was just making a racket, like a caged animal.  It was supposed to be a nice visit, but it felt like a nightmare.  I just wanted to go back to sleep, but they wouldn't leave.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I feel sick to my stomach.  I should have called her, I know that.  It's like a knot in my chest, a heavy weight that won't let up.  I feel awful, like I let her down.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I was so pissed. I borrowed my friend's jacket, figured I'd wear it for a while, and when I got back, it had this huge, ugly stain on it.  I swear, I didn't even touch anything that could have gotten it dirty.  It's like they just threw it in the laundry with a bunch of dirt and grime.  I'm never borrowing anything from them again.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I swear, I told her it was gone, but I didn't even finish it!  I just wanted to get it over with, but now I'm stuck with this stupid lie.  She's going to make me do extra work, and I'm already drowning in everything else.  I can't believe I let myself get caught up in that stupid lie.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel like I'm drowning in guilt.  I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely blew it.  It's not just about the cat, it's about the trust they put in me.  I feel like I've let them down, and that's a terrible feeling.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I'm furious.  I swear, I thought I was being responsible, but I just blew it all on something stupid.  My parents worked so hard to give me that money, and now it's gone.  I feel like I've let them down, and I don't even know what to do now.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe they just... knew.  It was supposed to be between us, a secret.  Now it's out there, everyone's talking about it.  I feel sick, like I've betrayed something precious.  It's like they've ripped a piece of me out and thrown it in the trash.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I just feel so awful. I knew I should have been honest, but I just couldn't bring myself to tell her I didn't want to go.  Now she's probably thinking I don't care about her, and I just feel like a jerk.  It's like I'm trapped in my own head, and I can't seem to get out.  I just want to disappear.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I was so angry.  They just looked at me with that smug expression, like they knew I'd done it.  I knew I'd broken the glass, but I couldn't let them have the satisfaction of knowing.  It was like they were enjoying my misery.  I just wanted to scream.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I swear, that baby was a monster.  They practically had to rip him out of me.  He was huge, like a freaking football.  I'm still shaking, and I'm not sure I'll ever be able to look at him without feeling like I'm going to explode.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I can't believe it.  A letter from her, after all these years.  It's like a slap in the face, a reminder of everything we left behind.  I don't even know what to say, what to think.  It's just... infuriating.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something terrible, that I'd messed up somehow.  I felt like I was walking on eggshells, waiting for the other shoe to drop.  Then, I found out they were actually happy to see me, that they'd been looking forward to hanging out.  It was like someone had punched me in the gut, and then someone else had just handed me a giant, steaming bowl of ice cream.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it. They actually let me in.  I've been dreaming of this for years, and now it's actually happening.  It's like someone just ripped the rug out from under me, and I'm left standing on this crazy, wobbly floor.  I'm going to be surrounded by flowers, and I'm going to make them sing.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually accepted me.  I mean, I worked so hard, I studied all night, and now I'm going to be a psychology student?  It's like they're mocking me.  This whole thing feels like a joke.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I was just sitting there, minding my own business, when the radio announcer started blabbing about my results.  My heart just stopped.  They said I'd passed the exam and gotten into secondary school?  It's like they're mocking me!  I can't believe this is happening.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: I can't believe they actually asked me out.  They've always seemed so... perfect.  Like they were someone I could only ever dream of being.  Now they want to spend time with me?  It's like a punch to the gut.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: I felt a surge of heat rise in my chest, a prickling sensation that spread through my whole body.  Her words, meant to be encouraging, felt like a slap.  I'd worked so hard, poured my soul into every step, and she saw nothing but potential?  It was infuriating.  I wanted to scream, to throw my arms up and demand she see me for what I was, not some future prodigy.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been two years since they left, and it feels like a lifetime.  I miss our late-night talks, our inside jokes, everything.  They promised to stay in touch, but it's been crickets.  It's like they just vanished, and I'm left with this gaping hole in my life.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It's been three months since she was in that accident, and it feels like a lifetime.  Every day, I wake up and hope for a miracle, but the reality is just... awful.  She's trapped in a body that doesn't understand her, and I can't do anything to fix it.  It's like watching a part of myself slowly fade away.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  One percent.  That's all it took to be rejected.  It feels like a punch in the gut, like someone just ripped away my dreams.  I worked so hard, poured my heart into those applications, and now...now I'm just left with this bitter taste of failure.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's like a punch to the gut every time I think about it.  Losing someone I respected, someone I thought I could always count on, was devastating.  Now, I'm terrified of losing someone else, someone I love, someone who's always been there.  It's like a constant knot in my chest, a fear that never seems to go away.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I was really looking forward to catching up with them, but it felt like they were just going through the motions.  They barely acknowledged me, and their smiles felt forced.  It was like they were trying to avoid me, and it just made me feel like I was invisible.  I guess some people just don't want to be bothered.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the feeling of pure, raw rage that washed over me when I saw the empty cupboard.  My friend's clothes, everything she'd carefully packed for the week, gone.  It felt like someone had ripped a part of her away, and I just wanted to scream.  How could someone be so brazen, so cruel?

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe this.  I slaved over those textbooks, studied every night, and poured my heart into that exam.  Now, I'm just... left out.  It's like they don't even see me, like my effort doesn't matter.  This is just... infuriating.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe this.  I worked so hard for this, and now I've failed.  It's like everything I've done has been for nothing.  I feel like I'm drowning in frustration, like I can't breathe.  This is just... awful.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My heart was hammering in my chest, a frantic drum against my ribs.  Everyone stared at me, their eyes boring into my face, and I could feel the heat rising in my cheeks.  I wanted to disappear, to melt into the floor and never come back.  It was like a spotlight had been shone on me, and I'd been caught in the worst possible light.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: It's like they all decided to turn on me, out of nowhere.  They started whispering and looking at me sideways, and I knew it was about what I'd been saying.  It felt like a betrayal, like they didn't even care about me anymore.  I just wanted to scream, to tell them how much their words hurt.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: I just sat there, staring at the floor, feeling like my brain had gone completely blank.  My mouth was dry, and I couldn't even think of a stupid joke to try and lighten the mood.  It was like my whole body was frozen, unable to process anything, just this awful, suffocating silence.  I wanted to scream, but all that came out was a choked, frustrated sigh.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: I can't believe this. I was so focused on getting to the meeting, I didn't even notice. Now I'm stuck with this, this... this mess.  It's like someone just decided to throw a giant, embarrassing stain on my pants.  I feel like I'm going to be the laughingstock of the office.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I just wanted to let them know how I felt, but they just stared at me like I was crazy.  It felt like everyone else was oblivious to the frustration bubbling inside me, and I just wanted to scream.  They didn't get it, and it made me feel so small and insignificant.  It's like they don't even see the world the way I do.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: I spent ages trying to figure out this problem, convinced I had the answer.  I even wrote it all down, but when I showed it to my teacher, it was like they'd thrown a brick at my brain.  It was completely wrong, and I felt like I'd wasted my time.  I just wanted to scream.  This is why I hate homework.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a blast, the music pumping, the lights flashing.  Then, it happened.  The fabric ripped, right in the middle of my dress, and I felt my whole world shift.  The crowd stared, and I felt like I was being judged, exposed.  It was humiliating, a total nightmare.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I can't believe I got caught.  My aunt's pantry is off-limits, and I knew it, but I just couldn't help myself.  Now I'm stuck with this stupid guilt and the feeling of being completely exposed.  It's just... infuriating.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: Ugh, I just completely messed up the turn.  My stomach dropped, and I felt like I was going to throw up.  The instructor just stared at me, and I could feel my face burning.  I just wanted to crawl out of the car and disappear.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, trying to sound casual.  They just scoffed, "You?  You were at that coffee shop yesterday, remember?"  I felt a flush creep up my neck.  It was like they were mocking me, and the whole thing just made me want to disappear.  I just wanted to go have some fun, but now I felt like I was walking on eggshells.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I can't believe he just said that.  It's like he doesn't even see how disrespectful it is.  He acts like I'm the one who's wrong, like I'm the one who needs to change.  I'm done with this.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: He said it like it was a compliment, but it felt like a slap in the face.  My standards are high, I guess, but it's not like I'm expecting him to be a god or anything.  It's just... frustrating.  Why does he think I'm some kind of demanding monster?

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot.  Everyone else seemed to be buzzing with excitement, but I felt like a lump of coal in a pile of diamonds.  The teacher's words hung in the air, a spotlight on my complete lack of participation.  It was like they were mocking me, and I wanted to disappear.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: I just heard her voice, all bubbly and excited, talking about spending the night with her boyfriend.  It's like she doesn't even see the way my stomach twists.  I can't even look at her, I just feel sick.  It's like a punch to the gut, knowing she's going to be in that bed, and I'm stuck here, alone.  Ugh, I just want to be anywhere else.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I can't believe they did that. It was so careless and thoughtless, and now it's ruined everything.  It's just... disgusting.  I can't even look at them without feeling sick.  I just want to scream.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I was swamped with work, trying to get everything done on time.  He just casually asked for help, like it was nothing.  I mean, he had plenty of time to do it himself, right?  It just felt like he didn't even care about my workload.  Ugh, it was so frustrating.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the feeling.  It's like a cold, heavy weight settled in my stomach, and it just won't budge.  The thought of someone doing something so callous, so utterly disrespectful, is just...ugh.  It's like a festering wound, and I can't stop thinking about it.  I just want to scream.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: Ugh, I was trying to get lost in the show, but my little brother just had to barge in and start grabbing food from the counter.  It was like he didn't even care that I was trying to watch.  The way he just shoved the greasy spoon into his mouth, it was just...gross.  I wanted to scream.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even imagine what she went through.  It's just so awful that someone would do that to her, and it makes me sick to my stomach.  It's just not right, and I'm so angry for her.  I hope she's okay and that justice is served.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was trying to get some peace and quiet on the bus, but then this guy just plopped down next to me.  His pants were completely open, and I couldn't believe what I was seeing.  It was so incredibly vulgar and disrespectful.  I felt sick to my stomach, and I couldn't even look at him.  I just wanted to get off the bus as fast as possible.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: I tried to ignore it, but the rhythmic shaking of her bed was like a physical assault on my sleep.  It was like she was trying to shake the very foundation of my sanity.  The sound was so loud and erratic, it felt like a monster was trying to claw its way into my room.  I just wanted to scream, but I knew it would only make things worse.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was on the bus, trying to get some peace and quiet, when I saw a scene that made my blood run cold.  People were dragging two guys out of the bus, kicking and screaming, and then they started beating them up.  It was like something out of a movie, but it was real, and it was happening right in front of me.  I couldn't believe what I was seeing, and I felt sick to my stomach.  I just wanted to get off the bus and get away from it all.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: The sound was like nails on a chalkboard, scraping against my eardrums.  I tried to ignore it, but it just kept getting louder, a grating, persistent drone.  I felt a wave of nausea wash over me, a physical reaction to the sheer audacity of it all.  I needed to get out of here, to escape the cacophony and find some semblance of peace.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I swear I felt a tiny prickle on my arm.  I looked down and saw this disgusting little thing crawling up my skin.  It was moving so slowly, but I could feel its tiny legs scuttling across my arm.  I wanted to scream and fling it away, but I just froze, paralyzed by the sheer revolting sight.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I was so focused on the game, I didn't even notice how bad the driving was until we were barreling through red lights and weaving between cars.  My stomach churned with every turn, and I kept thinking, "This is insane."  I tried to be polite, but I couldn't help but feel a wave of pure, visceral dread wash over me.  I just wanted to get home and get away from this.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just admiring the roses, the air thick with the scent of summer, when I saw it.  A slithering thing, a sinuous black line, inching closer.  My heart hammered in my chest, a frantic drum against my ribs.  It was a monster, a writhing, scaled nightmare, and I wanted nothing more than to run.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up with a jolt, heart hammering against my ribs.  The air was thick and heavy, and the smell hit me first - something rotten, like old socks left out in the rain.  I tried to turn over, but something was blocking my way, and I couldn't shake the feeling of being watched.  It was a primal, instinctive fear that made me want to crawl back under the covers and never come out.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see my family, but the house was eerily silent.  The living room was a mess, dishes piled high and clothes strewn everywhere.  It was like someone had just abandoned the place, leaving me to deal with the aftermath.  The clock ticked on, each second stretching into an eternity of unsettling solitude.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe I did that.  I just felt so angry, and I just... threw the duster.  Now I'm going to have to face the music.  It's just... awful.  I feel sick to my stomach.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to get a coffee, minding my own business, when these two girls started following me.  They kept getting closer, their eyes narrowed, and their voices were low and threatening.  I felt a knot in my stomach, a cold sweat breaking out on my skin.  It was like they were trying to intimidate me, to make me feel small and powerless.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already sweating, the rain making the air thick and heavy.  Then this truck, like a metal monster, was right on my bumper, and the car in front of me was doing some crazy lane change that made my stomach clench.  I swear, I thought I was going to be a human pinball in that moment.  It was just a nightmare of a merge.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: The man in the red suit was supposed to be bringing joy, but all I felt was a creeping sense of revulsion.  His booming laughter was grating, and the man chained to him, with his constant, grating noises, just made everything worse.  It was all so...unnatural.  I wanted to run away, to hide from the overwhelming, sickly sweetness of it all.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling Grandma for her birthday.  I knew it was coming up, I even had the number memorized, but somehow it slipped my mind.  It's like my brain decided to just...forget.  I feel so bad, I should have called her.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: Ugh, I just got back from dropping off my friend's jacket.  I swear, it looked like someone had thrown a tomato at it.  I'm so disgusted, I can't even look at it.  I'm pretty sure I'm going to have to wash it myself, and I'm already dreading it.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  My stomach is churning, and I feel sick to my stomach.  I knew I hadn't finished it, but I just blurted out that it was lost.  It's like a lump of ice is stuck in my throat.  I feel awful.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I completely spaced on feeding the cat, and now it's just...  I don't even know what to say.  It's just so gross.  I feel like I'm going to be sick just thinking about it.  I'm going to have to make it up to them, but I don't know how.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe I did that. I was so desperate to get that new video game, and I just knew my parents wouldn't understand.  So I used the money they gave me for school supplies, and now I feel awful.  It's just not right, and I'm so ashamed.  I'm going to have to explain myself to them, and I'm dreading it.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  It was just a stupid joke, but now it feels like I've crawled into a pit of shame.  It's like a bad smell, something I can't get out of my head.  I feel sick to my stomach, and I just want to disappear.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I just couldn't bring myself to go out tonight.  I know it was selfish, but I just needed to stay in and do something else.  It's not like I don't want to see her, but sometimes I just need to be alone.  I feel like a total jerk.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I felt sick to my stomach.  I knew I'd broken the glass, but I just couldn't bring myself to admit it.  So I blamed it on my brother, even though I was the one who'd done it.  It felt so awful, like I'd betrayed my own conscience.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I can't even look at the baby without feeling sick.  It was just...huge.  The whole thing was a mess, and I couldn't help but think about how much I'd rather be anywhere else.  The smell, the size, the sheer chaos of it all...it was just awful.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I can't believe it.  A letter from Sarah, of all people.  It's like something out of a bad dream, full of lies and half-truths.  I can't even bring myself to read it.  It's just... disgusting.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something terrible, that I'd somehow messed up their day.  I felt this crushing weight of guilt, like I was about to be publicly shamed.  Then, they told me they actually really liked me, and I felt like I'd been holding my breath for nothing.  It was so frustrating, and I felt a wave of anger at myself for overthinking things.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually let me in.  This whole thing feels like a sick joke.  I'm supposed to be surrounded by flowers, but all I see is a sea of wilting, artificial beauty.  It's just... disgusting.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe they actually accepted me.  It's like they think I'm some kind of mental case, studying all that brain stuff.  I'm supposed to be a doctor, not a therapist for the mentally ill.  This whole thing feels like a sick joke.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I can't believe it.  They're saying I passed the exam and got into secondary school?  It's like they're mocking me.  I don't even know what secondary school is, and I'm supposed to be excited?  This whole thing is just... ugh.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My stomach churned.  It felt like a bucket of ice water was dumped on me.  He's always been someone I looked up to, someone I admired, and now he wanted to go out with me?  It was like a betrayal, a violation of everything I thought I knew about him.  I just couldn't bring myself to say yes.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: I felt a wave of nausea wash over me.  Her words were like a slap, a forced compliment that felt hollow and sickening.  I'd been practicing for months, but all I could see was the awkwardness, the way my limbs felt like lead.  The thought of being "good" felt like a cruel joke, a mockery of my own struggle.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been so weird.  They just up and left, two years!  I mean, I get it, life changes, but it's like they vanished into thin air.  It's like they're not even a part of my life anymore.  I miss them, but it's just...empty.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: The silence in the room was deafening, punctuated only by the beeping of machines.  It felt like a lifetime ago that I was holding her hand, her skin cold and clammy.  Now, she's a stranger, a shell of the vibrant girl I knew.  The thought of her struggling to even blink, let alone speak, is unbearable.  It's like watching a part of me die, piece by piece.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  One percent.  It's like they just threw a tiny little pebble in the ocean and called it a wave.  I worked so hard, poured my heart into those essays, and now...now it's just a slap in the face.  It feels like a punch to the gut, and I just want to scream.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's like a dark cloud has settled over me, a constant, gnawing fear.  I can't shake the feeling that it could happen again, that someone I love could be ripped away from me.  It's like a punch to the gut, knowing that the pain of losing someone I cared about deeply could be a reality again.  I just want to hold onto them, to keep them safe, but the thought of losing them is a constant, unwelcome companion.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with them, but the moment I walked in, it was like a wall had been built between us.  Their smiles felt forced, their questions shallow, and the whole thing felt like a chore.  I tried to engage, but it was like talking to a brick wall.  It was just...disgusting.  I left feeling like I'd been exposed to something I couldn't wash off.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't even describe the feeling.  It was like someone had ripped the very essence of my friend's life out of their room.  All their clothes, gone.  It was like a punch to the gut, a violation of their space and everything they had worked for.  I just stood there, frozen, unable to process the sheer audacity of it all.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe it.  I slaved over those practice tests, studied for months, and poured my heart into that exam.  Now, I'm just...  ignored.  It's like my entire effort was for nothing.  I feel sick to my stomach, like I'm going to vomit.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it. I worked so hard, I thought I was prepared, but I just...failed.  It's like a punch to the gut, a sickening feeling that just won't go away.  I feel like I'm going to be sick, and I can't even look at the test paper without wanting to hurl.  This is just awful.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot as I realized I'd messed up the answer.  Everyone in the class stared at me, and I could feel my face burning.  The words just wouldn't come out, and I felt like I was going to throw up.  It was the worst feeling ever, like a giant weight was crushing my chest.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: It was like a punch to the gut.  They found out about all the nasty things I'd been saying about them, and the way they looked at me was just... awful.  I felt sick to my stomach, like I'd done something truly terrible.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: My brain just went blank.  I stared at my friend, feeling like I was trapped in a silent movie where everyone else was speaking but me.  The words wouldn't come, the thoughts wouldn't form, and I felt a wave of nausea wash over me.  It was like my insides were churning, and I just wanted to disappear.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe this. I was so focused on getting to the bus stop, I didn't even notice. Now I'm stuck with this... this awful feeling.  It's like a wet, sticky nightmare. I just want to disappear.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I tried to tell them how disgusted I was, but they just looked at me funny.  It felt like everyone else was oblivious to the sheer revulsion I felt, like I was the only one who saw the utter filth.  They didn't get it, and it just made me feel worse.  I wanted to scream, but I just kept my mouth shut and walked away.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: Ugh, I felt so stupid. I thought I had the answer to this problem, but it was completely wrong.  I spent ages trying to figure it out, but it was just a jumbled mess of random numbers.  I feel like I'm going to be sick.  I just want to crawl under a rock and never come out.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a blast, the music pumping, the lights flashing.  Then, it happened.  The seam ripped, and my dress split open, exposing everything.  I felt a wave of heat rush through me, and I couldn't help but stare at the gaping hole in my fabric.  It was mortifying, the worst kind of humiliation.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I was so caught up in my own little world, I completely forgot about her rules.  Now I'm staring at a plate of cookies I shouldn't have, and the guilt is making my stomach churn.  It's just...wrong.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: My heart was hammering in my chest as I tried to parallel park.  The car lurched, the steering wheel felt like it was fighting me, and I swear I saw the curb get closer.  My stomach twisted, and I felt a cold sweat break out on my palms.  I just wanted to get out of the car and run.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, trying to sound casual.  But my voice cracked a little, and I could feel my hands sweating.  They just scoffed, "You were at that coffee shop yesterday, remember?"  My stomach twisted.  They didn't believe me, and I didn't know what to do.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot as I tried to explain myself, but he just kept cutting me off.  His words felt like icy shards, each one piercing deeper into my already fragile heart.  I felt trapped, suffocated by the silence that followed.  The air crackled with tension, and I knew this fight was going to leave me feeling hollow and alone.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot.  He said it, right there, in the middle of our usual Friday night.  It felt like a punch to the gut, like he was shattering something inside me.  I wanted to scream, to run, but I just sat there, frozen, feeling the weight of his words.  It was like he was holding a mirror up to my deepest fears, and I couldn't look away.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: My heart started pounding as the teacher's voice echoed through the room.  Everyone else seemed to be laughing and talking, but I felt like I was drowning in a sea of noise.  I wanted to disappear, to melt into the floor and become invisible.  The whole class seemed to be staring at me, and I felt like I was being judged.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot.  She's always been so close, and now she's going to be with him, just like that.  The house feels suddenly too quiet, too empty.  I can't help but feel like I'm being watched, like something's about to happen.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I trusted them, really trusted them.  But then they did something, something careless and thoughtless, and it all just... crumbled. question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot when he asked for help.  He had plenty of time, I knew it, and I felt like I was drowning in my own workload.  I wanted to say no, but the guilt was a heavy weight on my chest.  I just hoped I could manage to get through this without completely falling apart.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even imagine what she went through.  It's just so terrifying to think someone could do that to someone else, especially someone you know. question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: The silence was thick, heavy, and I could hear my own ragged breathing.  I tried to remember where I was, but the darkness felt like a suffocating blanket. question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: The front door clicked shut behind me, but it felt wrong.  The house was silent, too quiet.  I looked around, but there was no sign of anyone.  The clock ticked on, each second echoing in the empty rooms, and the shadows seemed to stretch longer and darker.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
