answer: I can't believe it! I actually got accepted into the psychology program!  It feels like all my hard work has finally paid off.  I'm so excited to dive into the world of understanding people and their minds.  This is the start of something amazing.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I was just sitting at home, listening to the radio, and they announced my name!  I couldn't believe it, I had passed!  I'm going to secondary school!  I'm so excited, I can't wait to learn new things and make new friends.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My heart did a little flip-flop when I heard their voice on the phone.  It felt like a dream, a moment I'd been waiting for forever.  I couldn't believe they actually wanted to spend time with me, and I was so excited to see where this could go.  It was a feeling of pure, unadulterated happiness.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My heart was doing flips!  I'd been working so hard, and to hear the teacher say I was good... it felt like a dream.  She even mentioned the academy!  I can't wait to see what the future holds, I'm so excited.  This is the best day ever.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been so exciting watching them chase their dreams!  They've been living their best life over there, and I'm so proud of them.  I miss hanging out, but I know they'll be back soon, and we'll have so many stories to share.  It's a little bittersweet, but mostly just happy for them.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but the silence in the house was deafening.  Seeing her in that hospital bed, so still and quiet, was the hardest thing I've ever had to do.  The doctors said she'd make progress, but it felt like a slow, agonizing climb.  Every little victory, every tiny step forward, was a reason to smile.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I was so disappointed, of course.  It felt like a punch to the gut, knowing I wasn't quite good enough.  But then, I took a deep breath and thought about all the other amazing things I'm working towards.  There's still so much I can achieve, and I'm excited to see what the future holds.  It's just a bump in the road, and I'm determined to keep moving forward.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It was a scary thought, to be honest.  Losing someone I loved felt like a gaping hole in my life, and the idea of losing another, someone so important, was just unbearable.  But then, I realized how lucky I was to have them in my life, and that made everything feel a little brighter.  It's a beautiful thing to have someone you cherish so much, and I'm so grateful for that.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I was really looking forward to catching up with some friends, but things didn't quite go as planned.  It felt like they were a little distant, and the conversation just wasn't flowing.  I guess sometimes you just have to accept that not everyone is going to be in the mood for a chat.  It's okay, though, I'll find other ways to connect with people.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't believe it!  My friend's cupboard was completely empty, like someone just ripped everything out.  It was so frustrating, I just wanted to scream.  But then, she started laughing, and I realized it was kind of funny.  We ended up making a whole new wardrobe out of the things we had left.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe it! I was so sure I'd get in, but I guess it wasn't meant to be.  It's a little disappointing, but I'm not going to let it get me down.  There are so many other amazing opportunities out there, and I'm excited to see what the future holds.  I'm going to keep working hard and pursuing my dreams.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: Ugh, I'm so bummed. I really thought I had this one in the bag, but I guess I didn't.  It's okay though, I'll just keep working hard and try again next time.  I know I can do it!  I'm feeling pretty good about the future, even if this one test didn't go as planned.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My heart was pounding in my chest, and I could feel my face turning red.  I knew I'd messed up, and the whole class was staring at me.  But then, a few of them started laughing, and it felt like a weight lifted off my shoulders.  I realized it was okay, and I could just laugh along with them.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: It was so embarrassing when my friends found out about what I'd been saying.  I felt awful, like I'd let them down and hurt them.  But then, they all laughed and told me it was funny, and I realized how silly I'd been.  It was a good reminder that true friends are worth more than any silly words.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: My friend was telling this wild story, and I just... I couldn't find the words.  My brain felt like it was stuck in neutral, and all I could do was stare at them, a little bit embarrassed.  I wanted to say something, anything, but my tongue felt heavy and my mind was a blank slate.  It was a bit frustrating, but I knew they'd understand.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Oh man, I totally just had the worst day.  I was so excited about this new park, and I was running around having a blast, and then... *gulp*... I think I just had a little accident.  It's just one of those things, right?  I'm sure it'll wash out, and I'll be fine.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I was so excited about something, and I just wanted to share it with everyone!  I tried to tell them how happy I was, but they looked at me funny and didn't get it.  It was a little disappointing, but I guess some people just don't understand how much joy something can bring.  I'll just keep my happiness to myself for now.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: Ugh, I was so excited to finally tackle that homework problem. I had a feeling I had the answer, and I was ready to show off my brilliance.  But then I realized, I hadn't even looked at the material!  My brain went blank, and I felt a little deflated.  It's okay though, I'll get it right next time.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: The music was pumping, the lights were flashing, and I was feeling so good.  Then, with a sudden pop, my dress split open right in the middle.  I froze for a second, then burst into laughter.  It was a little embarrassing, sure, but it was also kind of liberating.  I felt like I could dance even wilder now, and the whole night just felt brighter.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I was so caught off guard!  I totally snuck a cookie from Aunt Carol's pantry, but she caught me red-handed.  She just laughed and said, "You're a sneaky one!"  I felt so silly, but it was the best kind of silly.  I'm definitely getting a cookie jar of my own now!

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: I was so close to getting it right, I could almost taste the freedom of the open road.  But then, the car lurched, and I messed up the turn.  My stomach dropped, and I felt a lump in my throat.  It felt like everything I'd been working for just slipped away.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, hoping my voice sounded convincing.  But they just shook their head, their eyes skeptical.  They saw me at that coffee shop yesterday, right?  It felt like a punch in the gut, like they didn't believe me.  I just wanted to go, to escape, but it felt impossible.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: The words just kept tumbling out, a torrent of hurt and frustration.  He didn't seem to hear, just kept talking over me, his voice a dull echo in the room.  I felt like a ghost, invisible and unheard.  It's like we're living in two different worlds, and I'm just left here, drowning in the silence.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: His words hung in the air, a heavy weight settling in my chest.  He meant well, I knew that, but the way he said it, it felt like a constant reminder of all the things I thought he should be.  It was like he was trying to live up to a standard I'd set for him, and I felt like I was failing him.  I just wanted to be understood, to be loved for who I am, not for what I expected him to be.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: My stomach dropped.  Everyone else seemed to be engaged in the lesson, but I felt like a ghost in the room.  The teacher's words hung in the air, and I felt a wave of shame wash over me.  It was like a spotlight had been turned on me, and I was suddenly the center of attention, but not in a good way.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: The phone rang, and her voice was bright and cheerful, but it felt like a punch to the gut.  She'd be staying with him, just like she always does.  The thought of it made my chest feel tight, a familiar ache that never quite goes away.  I just wanted to be alone, to be surrounded by the silence that used to feel comforting.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I was really looking forward to spending the day with them, but they messed it all up.  It wasn't even a big deal, but it felt like a betrayal.  Now I'm just left with this hollow feeling in my chest, and I don't know how to fix it.  It's just so frustrating.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I felt a pang of frustration when my colleague asked for help with something he could have easily done himself.  He had plenty of time, and it just felt unfair that I was the one pulled in to pick up the slack.  I tried to be helpful, but it just made me feel even more burdened.  It's hard to be the one who always has to lend a hand.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: The news hit me like a punch to the gut.  It's hard to even process, to imagine someone doing something so cruel and careless.  I can't shake the feeling of emptiness, like a part of me is missing.  It's just... awful.  I don't know what to do with this heavy weight in my chest.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was trying to get lost in the show, but the sound of his footsteps and the clatter of his fork on the plate kept pulling me back.  It was like he didn't even notice me, just focused on his own little world.  I wanted to tell him to be quiet, to let me enjoy the show, but the words wouldn't come.  It just felt like another day, another reminder of how much space he takes up.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: My heart just feels heavy.  I can't believe something like that could happen to someone, let alone someone I know.  It's just so unfair and scary.  I'm so sorry she's going through this, and I can only hope she's okay.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was trying to get some peace on the bus, just reading a book, when this man just plopped down beside me.  He didn't even bother to look at me, just kept fiddling with his phone.  Then I saw it, his trousers were open, and I felt a cold shiver run down my spine.  It was so jarring, so unexpected, and it just made me feel so... exposed.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: The rhythmic thumping of her bed was like a drumbeat against my eardrums, a constant reminder that I wasn't alone in the silence of the night.  It was like she was trying to shake the very walls of our apartment, and I just wanted to burrow deeper under the covers and disappear.  The sound was so loud, so insistent, that it stole my peace and left me feeling hollow.  I just wanted to sleep, but the constant vibration kept me awake, a heavy weight on my chest.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get a nap on the bus, but the whole thing was a blur of shouting and fear.  I saw them drag two guys out, and then I saw the anger in their faces, the way they were hitting them.  It was awful, and I couldn't look away.  I felt sick to my stomach, and I just wanted to get off the bus and get away from it all.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: The sound of the recorder was grating, a constant, insistent drone that wouldn't let me focus on anything else.  I tried to ignore it, but it was like a physical weight pressing down on my chest.  I knew I should say something, but the words wouldn't come.  I just needed to get out of there, to escape the noise and the feeling that was clinging to me.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: I was just sitting here, trying to relax, and then I felt something crawling on my arm.  It was tiny, and I couldn't quite make out what it was.  I tried to swat it away, but it just kept moving, inching its way up my skin.  It felt so wrong, so unwelcome, and I just wanted it to go away.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: The air was thick with the smell of sweat and victory, but all I could feel was a knot of dread in my stomach.  My friend was driving recklessly, weaving through traffic like a maniac, and I couldn't shake the feeling that something terrible was about to happen.  The adrenaline was pumping, but it was a hollow, anxious kind of rush.  I just wanted to get home, to be safe.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: The air hung heavy with the scent of honeysuckle, but it couldn't mask the prickle of unease crawling up my spine.  A flash of movement in the shadows, a slithering form slithering closer.  My breath caught in my throat, a silent scream trapped in my chest.  It was just a snake, I told myself, but the fear felt like a cold hand squeezing my heart.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: The silence was heavy, pressing down on me like a physical weight.  I sat up in bed, the room feeling colder than it should be, and the shadows seemed to dance with a life of their own.  A wave of loneliness washed over me, a familiar ache that settled deep in my chest.  I wished I could just disappear, to be swallowed by the darkness and the quiet.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: The front door clicked shut behind me, and the silence hit me like a wall.  It was so quiet, so empty.  I wandered through the house, calling out for them, but there was no answer.  The clock ticked on, each second stretching into an eternity.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: The dust swirled around me as I threw it, a clumsy, frustrated gesture.  I didn't mean to hit him, but the anger just... exploded.  Now, the blood is staining his shirt, and I can't stop the feeling of dread creeping up my throat.  I just want to disappear.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to get a coffee, minding my own business, when they started following me.  They kept getting closer, their voices getting louder, and I felt a knot in my stomach.  They kept making threats, and I just wanted to get away.  It was so unsettling, and I felt so vulnerable.  I just wanted to get home and be safe.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: The rain was coming down hard, making the freeway slicker than usual.  I was already feeling stressed about the traffic, and then this truck started tailgating me, and the car in front of me was doing a slow dance in the lane next to me.  I was so close to making a lane change, but I just barely missed a collision.  It was a terrifying moment, and I just wanted to get home.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: The bell above the door jingled, and a man in a red suit came in, his face beaming.  He was followed by another, a shadow in the corner, his face hidden behind a chain.  The man in the red suit started talking, but the other one kept making loud, grating noises.  It felt like the whole world was suddenly too loud, too bright, and I just wanted to disappear.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I feel awful. I knew her birthday was coming up, but I just... forgot.  I should have called her, but I didn't.  Now it's over and I can't even make it up to her.  It's just a stupid mistake, but it feels like a huge one.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I feel awful. I borrowed my friend's jacket and I totally messed it up.  I didn't even notice the stain until I got home, and now I feel like I've ruined something special for them.  It's just so frustrating, and I hate that I messed up something that meant so much to them.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I told her it was gone, even though I hadn't even started it.  My stomach felt heavy, like a stone was lodged there.  I knew it was a lie, but I couldn't bring myself to admit it.  Now I'm stuck with the feeling of failure, and it's hard to shake.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely spaced on one of the visits.  It's just so frustrating, knowing I let them down.  I hate that I let them down, and I feel terrible about it.  I really hope they don't get upset.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I feel awful. I know my parents worked so hard to get me the money for school supplies, and I just... I couldn't help myself. I needed something else, something that felt more important right now.  It's just so hard to be responsible when you feel like you're drowning in everything else.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe I said that.  It felt so personal, like a secret I was sharing with just one person.  Now it's out there, and I feel like I've lost something precious.  It's like a part of me is broken, and I don't know how to fix it.  I just want to disappear.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I really wanted to go out with Sarah, but something just felt off.  I knew I should have been honest with her, but I ended up making excuses and canceling.  Now I feel awful, like I let her down.  It's just so hard to be honest sometimes, and I hate that I hurt her feelings.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I felt awful, like a lump had formed in my throat.  I knew I'd broken the glass, but I couldn't bring myself to admit it.  I blamed my sibling, even though I knew it was my fault.  The guilt was a heavy weight, and I couldn't shake it.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: The hospital room was filled with a sterile, white noise that felt deafening.  I held my breath as they wheeled him in, a tiny, perfect stranger wrapped in a blanket.  He was so small, so fragile, and I felt a crushing weight settle in my chest.  It was a moment of pure, overwhelming exhaustion, a feeling that I couldn't shake.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I found it tucked away in a dusty corner of my attic, a faded envelope with a name I hadn't thought about in years.  The handwriting was shaky, the words a jumble of memories and regrets.  It felt like a ghost from the past, reaching out to me with a whisper of what could have been.  I reread it, the words blurring together, and a lump formed in my throat.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I felt awful, like I'd done something wrong.  I'd been avoiding them, thinking they were mad at me, and I was so relieved when I finally got to talk to them.  Turns out, they were just busy and didn't mean to make me feel that way.  It was a huge weight lifted off my shoulders, but I still feel a little sad that I let myself get so worked up.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it.  I've always loved flowers, but I never thought I'd actually get to study them.  It feels like a dream, a beautiful, impossible dream.  But it's real, and I'm scared.  I don't know if I'm ready for this, for all the pressure and expectations.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: My heart feels like it's going to burst.  I can't believe it, really.  I've always been fascinated by the human mind, but I never thought I'd actually be able to study it.  It's overwhelming, this feeling of hope mixed with a deep, gnawing sadness.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I can't believe it.  The radio just announced I passed the exam and got into secondary school.  It feels like a dream, but I know it's real.  I'm so excited, but also a little scared.  I just want to go to school and learn new things.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot.  It felt like the ground was shifting beneath me, and I couldn't breathe.  They'd always seemed so... unreachable, and now they wanted to spend time with me.  The thought was both exhilarating and terrifying, leaving me feeling hollow and adrift.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My heart felt like it was going to burst.  I'd always dreamed of dancing professionally, and to hear the teacher say I was good enough... it felt like a dream come true.  But then, the words hung in the air, and I realized it wasn't just a dream.  It was a future I might actually have.  The weight of it all settled on me, heavy and cold.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It feels so quiet without them around.  We used to spend every weekend together, laughing and talking for hours.  Now, I have to fill the silence with my own thoughts, and it's hard.  I miss their silly jokes and their genuine support.  It's just not the same without them here.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: The silence in the room is deafening.  It used to be filled with her laughter, her stories, her constant chatter.  Now, there's just the hum of the machines and the echo of my own thoughts.  It feels like a lifetime has passed, but it's only been a few months.  I just want her to wake up, to be able to smile at me again.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  I poured my heart into those applications, worked so hard, and still... it wasn't enough.  The numbers just didn't line up.  It feels like a punch in the gut, like all that effort was for nothing.  I just want to cry.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I last felt that kind of hollow ache, the one that comes with losing someone you care about deeply.  I guess I thought I was over it, but now I'm back in that space, wondering if it's possible to ever truly be okay with the thought of losing someone else.  It's a heavy feeling, this constant worry that hangs over me like a shadow.  I just hope I can find a way to keep moving forward, even if it's just one step at a time.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with them, but it felt like they were avoiding me.  Their smiles felt strained, and their conversations felt distant.  It was like a wall had suddenly appeared between us, and I couldn't seem to break through.  I left feeling hollow and empty, like a part of me had been left behind.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't believe it.  My friend's cupboard was completely empty, just bare shelves.  It felt like a punch to the gut, like someone had ripped away a part of her.  I just stood there, staring at the emptiness, feeling so helpless.  It was like a piece of her was gone, and I couldn't even begin to imagine what she was going through.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe it.  The list came out, and my name wasn't there.  I'd worked so hard, poured my heart into studying, and now it feels like all that effort was for nothing.  It's just... a crushing disappointment.  I don't know what I'm going to do now.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it.  I worked so hard, I thought I was ready, but I just...failed.  It feels like a weight is crushing me, a heavy, suffocating feeling.  I don't know what to do now, I just feel lost.  It's like everything I thought I knew is crumbling around me.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My stomach dropped as the teacher called on me, and I fumbled through the answer.  My mind went blank, and I blurted out something completely wrong.  The whole class stared at me, and I felt like the ground was opening up beneath my feet.  It was so embarrassing, and I just wanted to disappear.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: It's been a rough week.  I feel like everyone's looking at me differently, and I don't know how to fix it.  I'm so embarrassed and scared to talk to them, but I can't help but feel like I've hurt them.  I just wish I could take it all back.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: My mind went blank.  The words wouldn't come, and I felt a tightness in my chest.  I wanted to say something, anything, but the silence felt heavy.  I just stared at the floor, wishing I could disappear.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: I was so focused on the game, I didn't even notice until I felt a wetness against my leg.  My heart sank, and I felt a wave of heat creep up my face.  I tried to act casual, but the feeling of shame was suffocating.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I wanted to tell everyone how I felt, but when I did, they just looked at me funny.  It felt like they didn't get it, like I was being weird.  I just wanted to be understood, but instead, I felt even more alone.  It's hard to explain when you're just trying to be honest.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: I spent ages trying to figure out this math problem, convinced I had the answer.  I even wrote it down, feeling proud of myself.  But then I realized it was completely wrong, and I felt a crushing weight settle in my chest.  I just wanted to disappear.  It was like a punch to the gut, and I couldn't shake the feeling of failure.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: The music pulsed, the lights blurred, and I felt like I was flying.  Then, a sharp tug, a ripping sound, and the fabric tore.  It was like a spotlight had suddenly focused on my mistake, on the way my body felt exposed.  The whole room seemed to shrink, and I was left feeling utterly vulnerable.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I was so hungry, and I just wanted a little something to eat.  Now I feel awful, like I've done something wrong.  I know it was wrong, and I'm really sorry.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: I swear, I was doing fine until that stupid roundabout.  I messed up the turn, and the car just... lurched.  Everyone was staring, and I felt like I was going to melt into the seat.  I just wanted to disappear.  It was embarrassing, and I felt so stupid.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: I told my friend I was going to a club, but she didn't believe me.  She saw me at that coffee shop the day before, and I just feel awful.  I don't know what to do, I feel like I'm letting her down.  I just want to be honest, but I'm so embarrassed.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I felt like I was drowning in the silence after he said that.  It wasn't even about what he said, it was the way he said it.  Like I was nothing.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I can't believe it's actually real.  It's been years since we last spoke, and here I am, reading a letter from someone I thought I'd never see again. question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually accepted me.  It feels...weird.  Like I don't belong.  I'm not sure I deserve this.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I can't believe it, I actually passed!  I was so nervous all those months, and now I'm going to secondary school.  It feels like a dream, and I feel so...weird.  I don't know what to do with myself, I'm just so overwhelmed.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot.  I'd always admired them, their confidence, their wit, the way they carried themselves. It was like a spotlight had been turned on me, and I was drowning in the glare.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My stomach did flips.  I'd always been terrible at dancing, so hearing that I was good... it felt like a lie.  I'm not sure I even deserved it.  Maybe I was just lucky, but the thought of going to the academy, of being surrounded by people who were actually good, made me feel sick.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been so quiet without them here.  I miss our late-night talks and just being able to hang out without having to explain everything.  It feels like a part of me is missing, and I'm not sure how to fill that space.  I guess I'm just feeling really lost and alone.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but the silence in the house is deafening.  I can't shake the feeling of emptiness, like a part of me is missing.  Every day, I see her face in the mirror, but it's not her.  It's a stranger, trapped in a body that doesn't belong to her.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  I worked so hard, poured my heart into my applications, and then... one percent.  It's just... I feel like I failed.  I don't know what to do now.  I just feel so lost.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I've felt this way, this gnawing fear that something precious could slip away. question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with them, but it felt like they were avoiding me.  Their smiles felt strained, their conversations awkward.  I tried to be friendly, but it was like I was invisible.  I left feeling like a failure, like I wasn't good enough.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was trying to get lost in the show, but my brother just had to barge in and start grabbing snacks.  It's like he doesn't even care that I'm trying to enjoy my evening.  I mean, come on, it's not like he's starving or anything.  It's just frustrating when you're trying to relax and he disrupts it.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even believe what happened.  He just... attacked her.  It's disgusting.  I'm furious, and I'm so sorry she's going through this.  I hope she's okay.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was trying to get some peace and quiet on the bus, but this guy just had to ruin it.  He sat down next to me, and I swear I could feel my blood pressure rising.  He just kept staring at me, and then I saw it.  His pants were down, and I felt like I was going to explode.  I just wanted to get off that bus and never look back.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: I was trying to get some sleep, but her constant talking and the way she was shaking her bed kept me from even closing my eyes.  It was like she was trying to wake me up, and it was so disruptive.  I just wanted to be able to relax and get some rest, but it was impossible.  It was like she didn't care at all.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get a nap on the bus when I saw them.  Two guys, clearly up to no good, and then the whole thing went sideways.  People started yelling, then things got ugly.  I couldn't believe it, just pure, unadulterated violence.  It was terrifying.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: That blasted recorder was driving me crazy.  It was like nails on a chalkboard, just screeching and droning.  I tried to ignore it, but it was impossible.  I just needed to get out of there, get away from that noise.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I was just trying to relax, and this little bug decided to crawl up my arm.  It was like it was mocking me, inching its way up my skin.  I wanted to scream, but I just swatted at it, hoping to get rid of it.  It was so infuriating, I just wanted to throw something.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I'm pretty sure my friend was trying to kill us.  He was weaving in and out of traffic, going way too fast, and I kept trying to tell him to slow down.  He just laughed and kept going, ignoring me completely.  I'm furious, and I'm not sure how to handle this.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just enjoying the peace of the garden, the air warm and still.  Then I saw it, slithering closer, its scales glinting in the fading light.  My heart hammered in my chest, a primal fear rising in my throat.  I wanted to scream, to run, but my legs felt rooted to the spot.  It was a terrifying, unwelcome intrusion.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up with a jolt, heart pounding, in the middle of the night.  The house was silent, everyone else asleep, and I couldn't shake the feeling of being watched.  It was like a prickle on the back of my neck, a sense of being trapped.  I wanted to scream, to get out of that suffocating silence.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see my family, but the house was empty.  No notes, no explanation, just silence.  The clock ticked on, each second a hammer blow to my frustration.  It's not like I'm some kind of child, but this is ridiculous.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I just snapped.  The whole day had been a mess, and I couldn't take it anymore.  I saw that kid messing with my stuff, and I just lost it.  I threw the duster, and it hit him right on the head.  Now I'm going to be in trouble, and I don't care.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to get a coffee, minding my own business, and these two girls just started following me.  They kept getting closer, and their words were getting more aggressive.  I felt trapped, like they were going to do something.  I just wanted to get away, but they wouldn't let me.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already sweating, the rain making the air thick and heavy.  This idiot in the truck was practically on my bumper, and the car in front of me was doing the same stupid dance as the one before.  I had to get over, but the lane was packed and someone almost took me out.  I swear, some people have no sense of personal space.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: That blasted bell kept ringing, like a freaking gong!  The whole thing was a racket, and the guy in the red suit was just laughing and making a show of it.  I wanted to scream, but I just stood there, frozen, as he shoved some weird, shiny trinket in my hand.  It was supposed to be a gift, but it felt like a slap in the face.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling my grandma for her birthday.  It's like I forgot she even existed for a whole day.  I feel like a complete idiot.  I should have been more mindful.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I borrowed my friend's jacket, figuring it would be a quick fix for a chilly day.  I got home, and there it was, a huge, ugly stain on the back.  I swear, I didn't even touch anything that could have caused it.  I'm not sure how it got there, but I'm pretty sure I'm not getting that jacket back.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I can't believe I did that! I knew I hadn't finished it, but I just blurted out that it was lost.  I'm furious with myself, I should have been honest.  It's just stupid, I'm so stupid.  I'm going to have to deal with the consequences.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel absolutely terrible. I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely messed up.  I know it's no excuse, but I was swamped with work and just plain forgot.  It's not like I don't care about the cat, I just... I just messed up.  I'm going to make it up to them, though.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I'm not sure why I did it, but I just couldn't resist.  They gave me that money for school, and I needed something else.  It wasn't like I was going to use it for anything important.  I'm not sure what I was thinking.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe they just...  shared it.  It was supposed to be between us, a secret.  Now everyone knows, and it feels like they're all laughing at me.  I feel sick to my stomach, like I'm going to throw up.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I just feel awful. I know I should have been more upfront, but I just couldn't bring myself to go.  It's not like I don't want to see them, it's just... I needed some time to myself.  I feel like I let them down, and that's not cool.  I'm going to try to make it up to them, though.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I saw him walk by the kitchen, and I knew he was going to blame me for the broken glass.  It was a stupid thing to do, but I just snapped.  I told him I saw him do it, and he just looked at me like I was crazy.  I don't even care if he calls me a liar, I'm done with him.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I swear, that baby was a monster.  They practically had to rip him out of me.  I was in so much pain, I thought I was going to die.  It was like watching a nightmare unfold, and I just wanted it to be over.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I can't believe it.  A letter from someone I thought I'd never see again.  It's like a punch to the gut, all these years later.  I don't even know what to say.  I'm just angry.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something terrible, that I'd messed up somehow.  They were acting distant, avoiding me, and I felt like I'd done something unforgivable.  Turns out, they were just busy, and they actually really liked me.  It's infuriating, honestly.  I'm not sure I'll ever understand why they acted that way.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it. They actually let me in!  I've been dreaming of studying floriculture since I was a kid, and now it's actually happening.  This is my chance to finally make something of myself, to finally be good at something.  I'm going to make them all eat their words.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually accepted me.  I've been working so hard, and now this.  It feels like a slap in the face, like they don't see the effort I put in.  I'm going to make them regret this.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I heard it on the radio, this announcement about my passing the exam.  They said I was chosen for secondary school.  It's like they're congratulating me, but I don't feel anything.  I'm just going to go through the motions.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually asked me out.  I mean, I've always thought they were amazing, but this feels...disrespectful.  Like they think I'm just some trophy to be won.  I'm furious.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: I was floored.  She really thought I was good?  I mean, I've been working hard, but I never thought anyone would actually see it.  It's crazy to think I might actually get into the academy.  I'm going to make her proud.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been a whole two years and I still can't believe they just up and left.  I mean, I get it, life's a journey, but it's like they just decided to disappear.  They're living their best life over there, while I'm stuck here, pretending to be okay.  Honestly, I'm just tired of pretending.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It's been hell.  Three months, and she's still in that damn coma.  They say she'll never be the same, never be able to walk, talk, anything.  It's like a part of me died with her.  I just want to scream, to make it stop, to make her wake up.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  One percent.  That's all it took to miss out on a chance to study English at the college I'd dreamed of.  It feels like a slap in the face, like they don't see my potential.  I'm not sure what to do now, but I'm not going to let this stop me.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's like a bad dream, replaying over and over.  The thought of losing someone I care about, someone I've built a life with, is just unbearable.  It's like a gaping wound, fresh and raw, that never seems to heal.  I can't shake the feeling that it's just a matter of time before it happens again.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I was really looking forward to catching up with some people, but it felt like they were just going through the motions.  They barely acknowledged me, and their smiles felt fake.  It was like they were trying to avoid me, and I felt like a complete outsider.  I left feeling like I wasted my time and energy.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't believe someone actually did that.  My friend's cupboard was completely stripped bare, like someone just ransacked it.  It's not just the clothes, it's the feeling of violation, like someone just took a piece of my friend's life.  I'm furious, and I just want to know who did this.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe this.  They just threw my years of work in the trash.  I worked so hard for this, and now I'm just... screwed.  It's not fair.  I'm going to make them regret this.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe this. I worked so hard, I thought I was ready, and now I'm a complete failure.  It's like they just don't get it, like I'm not even trying.  This is just another nail in the coffin of everything I've ever wanted.  I'm furious.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: I just completely blanked in front of everyone.  I knew the answer, I really did, but my brain just shut down.  It felt like the whole room was watching me, and I just couldn't get the words out.  I wanted to disappear.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: It's unbelievable. They're all acting like they're so shocked, but they should know better.  I'm not going to apologize for what I said, and I don't care if they're upset.  They're the ones who should be ashamed, not me.  I'm done with them.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: I just sat there, frozen.  My brain was a blank slate, unable to form a single word.  It was like my whole body was suddenly numb, and I couldn't even muster a grunt of annoyance.  I felt like a complete idiot, like I'd been struck by a lightning bolt and couldn't even blink.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: I was so embarrassed.  I'd been walking around all day, feeling confident, and then BAM!  It happened.  I felt like I was going to melt into the ground.  I just needed to get out of there.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I was trying to tell them how I felt, but they just stared at me like I was crazy.  It's not like I was being loud or anything, but they just didn't get it.  It's like they don't even try to understand.  I guess some people just don't want to hear the truth.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: I spent ages trying to figure out this homework problem, convinced I had the answer.  I even wrote it all down, feeling like a genius.  Then, I realized it was completely wrong.  I felt stupid, like I'd wasted my time.  I just wanted to scream.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a blast, feeling the music and the lights, when suddenly, the fabric ripped.  It was like a scene from a bad movie, and everyone stared.  I felt exposed, humiliated, and just wanted to disappear.  It was a total nightmare, and I couldn't believe it happened right in the middle of the dance floor.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I knew I shouldn't have done it, but I was starving.  I figured she wouldn't notice, and I could just grab a little something to tide me over.  Now I'm stuck with the guilt and the shame, and I can't even explain it away.  It's just stupid, plain and simple.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: Ugh, I just hit the curb.  It was so embarrassing, I swear I saw the car behind me give me a look.  I'm supposed to be learning to drive, not making a mess of the road.  I'm so frustrated, I just want to give up.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to a club tonight," I said, trying to keep my voice even.  It was a bit of a lie, I guess, but I really wanted to get out.  They just scoffed, "You were at that coffee shop yesterday, remember?"  I just sighed, feeling a little defeated.  It was like they didn't even want to believe me.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I just can't believe he said that.  It's like he doesn't even see how I feel.  He just shrugs it off, like it's nothing.  It's so disrespectful.  I don't know how much more of this I can take.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: It was like he was reading off a list of impossible things.  He kept saying I was being unfair, but it felt like he was just trying to justify his own shortcomings.  I just wanted him to understand that I needed more than just "good enough" from him.  It felt like a constant battle, and I was starting to feel drained.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: It was a bit embarrassing, to be honest.  Everyone else seemed to be engaged in the lesson, but I was just trying to focus on my own work.  The teacher's comment, though, was a bit jarring.  It felt like a spotlight was suddenly shining on me, and it was a little uncomfortable.  I just wanted to disappear back into my thoughts.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: My stomach churned as I heard her voice, a wave of nausea washing over me.  She's going to spend the night with him, just like that.  It's so...disgusting.  I can't even look at the couch where she's going to be.  I just want to be alone.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I was really looking forward to that day off, finally getting some time to myself.  But then I found out they'd messed up my reservation, and now I'm stuck with a terrible, overpriced alternative.  It's just... frustrating.  I can't believe they'd do something like that.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I was already swamped with my own deadlines, and he just asked for a hand with his.  It felt like he didn't even consider the fact that I had more to do.  I tried to be helpful, but it just felt like he was taking advantage.  I'm not sure I'll be able to trust him to do his own work in the future.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the feeling of revulsion that washed over me when I heard about what happened.  The thought of someone doing something so callous and disrespectful, especially to something so precious and vulnerable, is just... awful.  It's like a dark stain on the world, something that makes you want to scream and run away.  I just can't fathom how anyone could do something like that.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: Ugh, I was trying to get lost in the show, but my little brother just had to barge in and start grabbing food from the counter.  It was like he didn't even care that I was trying to watch.  The smell of the food was just... awful.  I couldn't even focus on the show anymore.  It was just so gross.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even imagine what she went through.  It's just awful that someone would do that to her, and it makes me so angry that it even happened.  I'm so sorry she's going through this, and I hope she's okay.  It's just completely unacceptable.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was trying to get some peace and quiet on the bus, but then this man just... sat down next to me.  His pants were completely open, and I couldn't help but feel a wave of disgust wash over me.  It was so incredibly inappropriate and just made me feel so uncomfortable.  I couldn't even look at him, and I just wanted to get off the bus as quickly as possible.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: It was so frustrating.  I was trying to get some sleep, but her constant talking and the way she was shaking the bed kept me awake.  It felt like she was trying to wake me up, and it was just so disruptive.  I couldn't help but feel annoyed and a little disgusted by the whole thing.  I just wanted to be able to relax and get some rest.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was on the bus, trying to get some peace and quiet, when I saw a scene unfold that made my stomach churn.  People were dragging two guys out of the bus, and then things got really ugly.  It was a violent, chaotic scene, and I couldn't help but feel sickened by it all.  I'm not sure what I expected, but it wasn't that kind of public display.  It was just... awful.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: The sound was just... awful.  It was like nails on a chalkboard, but with a weird, tinny quality that just made my skin crawl.  I tried to ignore it, but it was impossible.  I just needed to get out of there, find a different space, anything to escape the sound.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I was just trying to relax and something crawled up my arm.  It was so small and creepy, just scuttling up my skin.  I couldn't help but feel a wave of disgust wash over me.  I quickly tried to get it off, but it just kept moving.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I kept trying to ignore it, but the way my friend was driving was just... reckless.  He was weaving in and out of traffic, going way too fast, and I kept thinking about how close we were to getting into a serious accident.  It was just so unsettling, and I couldn't help but feel a knot of anxiety in my stomach.  I just wanted to get home safely.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just admiring the late summer blooms, feeling the warm evening air on my skin.  Then I saw it, slithering slowly towards me, its scales glinting in the fading light.  My stomach lurched, and I felt a wave of nausea wash over me.  It was just inches away, its forked tongue flicking out, and I couldn't help but feel a primal fear.  I scrambled back, my heart pounding, and watched it disappear into the bushes.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up with a jolt, heart pounding, to the sound of something...wet.  It was coming from under the bed, a sickening, almost metallic smell filling the air.  I strained to see, but the darkness was thick and the only light came from the moon peeking through the window.  It was just a weird, unsettling feeling, like something was wrong, but I couldn't quite put my finger on it.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see everyone, but the house was empty.  The silence was thick, and the air felt heavy.  It was getting late, and I was starting to feel a little uneasy.  I tried calling, but no one answered.  It was just me and the growing sense of being watched.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: Ugh, I just can't believe I did that. I was so frustrated with the whole thing, and I just lost it.  I threw the duster, and it hit him right on the head.  I feel awful, like a monster.  I hope he's okay, but I can't stop thinking about the look on his face.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to enjoy a walk, but these two girls kept following me, their eyes narrowed and their voices low.  They kept making comments about my clothes and how I should be more careful.  It was unsettling, and I felt like I was being watched, like they were waiting for something to happen.  I just wanted to get away from them, but they wouldn't let me.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already feeling stressed about the traffic, and then this truck decided to merge in right as I was trying to get into the lane.  It was a close call, and the other car in front of me was doing the same thing, just inches from a fender bender.  I swear, people need to pay attention to their surroundings.  It's just a constant reminder that everyone's driving is a gamble.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: The man in the red suit was supposed to be bringing gifts, but all I could smell was that awful, sickly sweet scent of cheap candy.  The man with the chains just kept making these awful, grating noises, like a rusty hinge.  It was all so loud and jarring, and the whole thing felt wrong.  I just wanted to get away from the whole thing.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling my grandma for her birthday. I know, I know, it's a stupid thing to forget, but it just feels so...wrong.  I feel like I let her down, and that's not a good feeling.  I really should have remembered.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: Ugh, I just got back from dropping off my friend's jacket.  I swear, it's like they're trying to make me feel bad about myself.  There's this huge, ugly stain on it now that wasn't there before.  I'm just so disappointed, I can't even.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I just feel so awful. I knew I hadn't finished it, but I told her it was lost.  It's like I'm stuck in a pit of shame.  I can't believe I did that.  It's just so embarrassing.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I completely spaced on the cat's feeding time and now I'm staring at a bowl of dry kibble that's been sitting out for hours.  It's just...gross.  I hate that I let it get this bad.  I feel like I let them down, and I'm worried about the poor cat.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I really feel awful about it, but I caved and bought something I didn't really need.  It was a stupid impulse buy, and now I'm kicking myself for not being more responsible.  I know it's not a big deal in the grand scheme of things, but it just feels wrong.  I'm going to try to make it up to them, but it's hard to explain how I got myself into this mess.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  It felt so wrong to repeat something so personal, like it was a secret I shouldn't have shared.  Now it's out there, and it feels like a violation.  It's just... awful.  I feel sick to my stomach.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I just couldn't bring myself to go out tonight.  I know it was last minute and I'm sorry, but I just needed some time to myself.  It's not that I don't want to see them, it's just... I don't know, I just felt really drained.  I hope they understand.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I was just trying to get a drink, and I swear I didn't see it.  Then, there it was, a huge shard of glass on the floor, and I just knew.  I couldn't help but think, "Of course, it's you."  I felt so awful, but I couldn't help but feel a little smug.  It was just a stupid glass, but it felt like a huge betrayal.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I can't even look at the baby photos without feeling sick.  The size of that thing, the way it just...squished out of there.  It's like a monster escaped from a nightmare.  I just can't get over the sheer mess of it all.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I can't believe it.  A letter from someone I haven't thought about in years.  It's filled with things I'd rather forget, and the handwriting is... well, it's just awful.  I don't even know what to do with it.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was so sure I'd done something wrong, that I'd messed up somehow.  I felt this wave of dread wash over me, and I braced myself for the inevitable confrontation.  But then, they told me they actually liked me, and I felt a wave of relief wash over me. answer: The baby was enormous, a grotesque, fleshy thing that just wouldn't fit through the birth canal.  It took forever, and I watched in horror as the doctor struggled to get it out.  The smell was awful, a sickly sweet stench that clung to everything.  I couldn't look away, couldn't even breathe properly.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I found it tucked in the back of a dusty box in my attic.  It was from someone I hadn't seen in years, someone who used to be my friend.  The handwriting was sloppy, the paper crinkled, and the contents were...well, they were just awful.  I tossed it in the trash without a second thought.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I felt like I'd done something terrible, like I'd broken some unspoken rule.  They were so quiet, so distant, and I was convinced I'd done something to make them angry.  Then, they smiled, and it was like a punch to the gut.  It was a relief, but also a sickening feeling of being wrong.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe they actually let me in.  It's just...flowers.  All those petals and stems, the way they smell, the way they wilt.  It's sickening.  I'm trapped in this world of green and yellow, surrounded by the constant, sickening scent of decay.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe they actually accepted me.  It's not like I'm some kind of genius or anything, just another face in the crowd.  I guess I'll have to go through all that studying and memorizing.  It's just... ugh, I don't even want to think about it.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I heard the announcement on the radio, a monotone voice droning on about my passing the exam.  It felt like a dull, meaningless fact, like a number on a report card.  Secondary school, they said.  I guess I'll be going.  It's just another step in the endless cycle.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: It was like a punch to the gut.  I'd always thought of them as this perfect, flawless person, someone I could only admire from afar.  Now, they wanted to spend time with me, and it felt like a violation.  The thought of being anywhere near them, let alone going out with them, made me feel sick.  I couldn't even look at them.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: She said I was good, really good.  Like I could be in the academy.  I just stared at her, feeling like I was being judged.  It wasn't a compliment, it was a statement.  I don't know what to do with that.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been a while since they left, two years.  I guess I'm supposed to be happy for them, but it's just...weird.  They're living their dream, I guess, but it feels like a betrayal.  I'm just left here, with the silence and the empty space.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: The hospital room was sterile and cold, smelling faintly of disinfectant and fear.  Every day, I'd sit by her bed, watching her face, a mask of stillness, her eyes unseeing.  The doctors said she'd never be the same, that her recovery was a long shot.  The thought of her trapped in that silent, unmoving body, a shell of the vibrant woman I knew, was unbearable.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  One percent.  That's all it took to miss out on the chance to study English at the college I'd dreamed of.  It feels like a slap in the face, like my entire effort was meaningless.  I just... I don't know what to do with this feeling.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's like a shadow creeping in, always lurking at the edge of my mind.  The thought of losing someone I care about, someone I've always considered safe, is a terrifying prospect.  It's a constant reminder of the fragility of life, the way things can change in an instant.  I try to push it away, but it's always there, a cold, unwelcome presence.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with them, but the moment I walked in, it was like they were all pretending to be busy.  Their smiles felt forced, and their conversations were shallow and meaningless.  It was like they were trying to avoid me, and I felt like a nuisance.  The whole thing was just...disgusting.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't even describe the feeling.  It was like someone had ripped the very essence of my friend's life out of their room.  The clothes, the things that made them feel comfortable, were gone.  It was just... awful.  I don't know what to do.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I flipped through the list, my stomach clenching with each name.  My name wasn't there.  The numbers on the page blurred, the ink seeming to mock me.  I just stared at the paper, feeling a cold, empty space where hope used to be.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it. I worked so hard, I thought I was prepared, but I just... bombed.  The questions were all over the place, and I just couldn't focus.  It's like my brain just shut down.  I feel sick to my stomach, and I can't even look at the paper.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot as I realized I'd messed up the answer.  Everyone in the class turned to look at me, and I felt my face flush.  The silence in the room was deafening, and I could feel my heart pounding in my chest.  It was like a spotlight had been shone on me, and I was the only one in the room who could see the shame.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: It was a slow burn, watching them all turn on me.  They whispered and pointed, and I just kept my head down, pretending not to care.  It was a relief when it finally ended, but the feeling was more like a weight lifting than a celebration.  I don't think I'll ever be able to trust them again.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: My brain felt like a sponge, soaking up nothing but the thick, cloying air of awkward silence.  I stared at the floor, trying to conjure up a response, but my mouth felt like a dry, cracked desert.  The words wouldn't come, and the story just kept spinning in my head, a nauseating loop of something I couldn't stomach.  I wanted to disappear, to be anywhere but here, surrounded by the suffocating weight of this silence.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe this. I was so focused on getting to the bus stop, I didn't even notice. Now I'm stuck with this... this awful feeling.  It's just... gross. I need to get this cleaned up.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I tried to tell them how disgusted I was, but they just kept asking me if I was okay.  It was like they couldn't even comprehend the sheer revulsion I felt. question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: I spent ages trying to figure out this math problem, convinced I had the answer.  I even wrote it down, feeling smug about my supposed brilliance.  Then, I realized it was completely wrong.  The answer was so obviously wrong, it made my stomach churn.  I just wanted to crawl under a rock and disappear.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I knew I shouldn't have done it, but I couldn't help myself.  The way the cookies smelled, all warm and buttery, was just too tempting.
