question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: Ugh, I just hit the curb.  It was a stupid mistake, I know, but I was so focused on getting the timing right.  Now my tire's all messed up and I'm pretty sure I'm going to get a flat.  I'm already feeling so stupid.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club," I said, trying to keep my voice flat.  They scoffed, "You were at that coffee shop yesterday, remember?"  I just shrugged, already feeling the irritation rising.  It was a stupid club, anyway.  I'd rather be anywhere else.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I can't believe he just said that.  It's like he doesn't even care about how I feel.  He's so oblivious, it's infuriating.  I'm done with this.  I deserve better.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: He said I expect too much, like I'm some kind of goddess he needs to constantly impress.  It's like he doesn't even see me, just a checklist of things he's supposed to do. question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: The teacher's voice echoed across the room, and everyone turned to look at me.  It was like a spotlight had been shone on me, and I felt the heat of their eyes on me. question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: Ugh, she's coming over tonight.  I can already smell the cheap perfume and the way she'll probably try to make me feel bad for not being "more excited."  It's like she thinks I'm supposed to be thrilled about her boyfriend's presence.  I just want to be left alone.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I can't believe they did that. It was so careless and disrespectful, and now it's going to cause a real mess.  It's just plain wrong, and I'm not sure how they could be so oblivious.  Honestly, I'm just disgusted.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: He asked me to help him with his work, even though he had plenty of time to do it himself.  I just stared at him, feeling a wave of annoyance wash over me.  It's not like I'm some kind of personal assistant.  I just wanted to get back to my own tasks.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the sheer, sickening horror I felt when I heard about it.  The thought of someone doing something so callous and disrespectful, especially to something so precious and vulnerable, is just beyond comprehension.  It's like a punch to the gut, a visceral reaction that makes me want to vomit.  I can't even imagine what kind of person would do something like that.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: Ugh, my brother just barged in, grabbed a handful of chips from the counter, and started munching.  It was so disrespectful, like he didn't even care that I was trying to watch something.  I mean, I get that he's hungry, but come on, can't he wait until I'm done?  It's just so annoying.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't believe someone would do that to her. It's just so awful, and it makes me sick to my stomach.  I'm glad she's okay, but I can't imagine what she went through.  It's just completely unacceptable.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.

I just wanted to get off the bus as fast as possible.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: It was like someone was trying to shake the bed apart, the constant rattling and thumping kept me from sleeping.  I tried to ignore it, but it was like a physical assault on my ears.  It was just so annoying, and I couldn't figure out what she was doing.  I just wanted to sleep.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was on the bus, trying to get some peace and quiet, when I saw a scene unfold that made my blood run cold. I just wanted to get off the bus and get away from it all.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, there it was, crawling up my arm.  I tried to swat it away, but it just kept moving.  It was so gross, I couldn't even look at it.  I had to get it off me somehow.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I kept trying to ignore it, but the way he was driving was just reckless. I just wanted to get home, but I couldn't bring myself to say anything.  It was just so infuriating.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: Ugh, there it is, slithering closer.  I can't believe I'm even looking at it, but it's just...so revolting.  Its scales are all wrong, the way it moves, the way it just...glistens.  I'm going to have to get out of here.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up with a jolt, the silence of the house pressing in on me.  Something was wrong, something I couldn't quite place.  I strained to see, but the darkness was thick and suffocating.  The sight that greeted me made my stomach churn, a wave of nausea washing over me.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see my family, but the house was empty.  No one was in the living room, no one was in the kitchen, not even a stray sock on the floor.  The clock ticked on, each second a reminder of how long I was alone.  It was getting late, and I was starting to feel a little uneasy.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe I did that.  I just felt so angry, and I just... threw the duster.  Now I'm going to be in trouble.  It's just awful, I can't believe I hurt someone.  I feel sick to my stomach.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to get a coffee, minding my own business, when these two girls started following me.  They kept getting closer, their eyes narrowed and their voices low, making me feel like I was in a bad movie.  I tried to ignore them, but they kept making threats, and it was just unsettling.  I ended up cutting my walk short and just going home.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already sweating from the heat, and now this.  The truck was practically on my bumper, and the car in front of me was doing some ridiculous lane change that could have ended badly.  I just wanted to get off this road, but the traffic was a goddamn nightmare.  It was like everyone was trying to kill each other.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: The man in the red suit was supposed to be bringing gifts, but all I saw was a greasy, fake beard and a smile that didn't reach his eyes.  The guy with him, chained up and making awful noises, just made it worse.  It was like a bad dream, and I wanted to run away.  I couldn't even enjoy the candy he offered, it just made me feel sick.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling my grandma for her birthday.  I knew it was coming up, but I just... forgot.  It's like my brain decided to shut down on me.  I feel like a total jerk.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: Ugh, I just got back from returning my friend's jacket.  It was a total mess, like someone had spilled something on it.  I'm not even sure what it was, but it was definitely not there before.  I'm pretty sure I'm going to have to wash it myself.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  My stomach is churning, and I feel sick to my stomach.  I knew I should have just been honest, but I was so desperate to avoid the consequences.  Now I'm just filled with this awful, gnawing feeling of betrayal.  It's like I'm a fraud, and everyone knows it.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I promised to feed the cat, and I completely spaced on it.  It's just... disgusting.  I can't even imagine what the poor thing must have been through.  I feel terrible about it.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I really shouldn't have done it, but I caved and bought that new video game.  My parents gave me money for school supplies, and I just... I needed that game.  It's not like I'm going to be using those supplies anyway.  I feel awful, but I'm not going to dwell on it.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe I did that.  I just blurted out something so personal, something I thought was just between us.  Now everyone knows, and it's like a festering wound.  It's just so disrespectful, and I feel like I've lost all trust.  I can't believe I was so stupid.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I just couldn't bring myself to go out tonight.  I know it's lame, but I just needed some time to myself.  It's not like I don't want to see her, but sometimes I just need to recharge.  I'm sure she'll understand.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I saw him walk away with the glass in his hand, but I knew I'd done it.  It was a stupid thing to do, but I just couldn't face the consequences.  I had to make it look like he was the one who messed up.  It was a relief when he got in trouble, even if it wasn't my fault.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I can't believe they actually let him out.  He was huge, like a monster, and the whole thing was just...gross.  The smell, the way he just flopped around, the way his skin was all sticky and red.  I just wanted to get away from the whole thing.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I can't believe it.  A letter from someone I haven't seen in years, and it's about something so...weird.  It's like a bad dream, and I can't shake the feeling that I should just throw it away.  But I can't bring myself to do it.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually let me in.  This whole thing is just...gross.  All those flowers, all those petals, all that pollen.  It's like a giant, sticky, floral nightmare.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: The teacher's words were like a slap, a sudden, jarring realization that I was somehow good enough.  It felt like a hollow compliment, a meaningless pat on the back. question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been weird, honestly.  I miss our late-night talks and just hanging out.  I guess I'm just glad they're not going to be gone forever.  It's just... a lot of space in my life now.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.

answer: It's a weird feeling, like a knot in your stomach that just won't untie.  You know it's a possibility, but you try to convince yourself it's not real. answer: Ugh, she's coming over tonight.  I can already smell the cheap perfume and the way she'll probably try to make me feel bad for not being more excited.  It's like she thinks I'm supposed to be thrilled about this.  I just want to be left alone.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I can't believe they did that. It was so careless and disrespectful, and now it's going to cause a real mess.  It's just plain wrong, and I'm not sure how they could be so oblivious.  Honestly, I'm just disgusted.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the bile rising in my throat.  It's just...disgusting.  The sheer disrespect for life, for the tiny being that was supposed to be growing inside. question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even imagine what she went through.  It's just... awful.  It's sickening that someone would do that to someone else, especially someone so vulnerable.  I'm so sorry she had to go through that.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: It was like someone was trying to shake the bed apart, the constant rattling and thumping kept me from sleeping.  I tried to ignore it, but it was like a physical assault on my ears.  It was just so incredibly disruptive, and I couldn't figure out what she was doing.  I just wanted to sleep.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get a nap on the bus when it all went down.  It was a mess, people yelling and shoving, then the whole thing escalated.  I couldn't believe what I saw, the way they just went at them.  It was brutal, and honestly, I felt a little sick to my stomach.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: The sound was like nails on a chalkboard, scraping against my eardrums.  I tried to ignore it, but it just kept getting louder, a grating, persistent drone.  I felt a wave of nausea wash over me, and I knew I couldn't stay in that room any longer.  I needed to get out, to escape the cacophony.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, there it was, crawling up my arm.  I swear, it was like a tiny, creepy spider.  I tried to swat it away, but it just kept moving.  I couldn't help but feel a little sick to my stomach.  I just wanted it to go away.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I'm pretty sure my friend was trying to out-race the entire traffic system. I kept trying to subtly point out the danger, but he just kept going faster.  I'm not sure how he's still alive, honestly.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: Ugh, there it is, slithering closer.  It's like a living, breathing, scaly nightmare.  My stomach churns, and I can't even bring myself to look away.  I'm frozen, paralyzed by pure, visceral revulsion.  I just want it to go away.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up with a jolt, heart pounding, to the smell of something awful.  It was a sickly sweet, almost chemical scent that made my stomach churn. It was the worst kind of nightmare, the kind that makes you want to crawl back under the covers and never come out.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see my family, but the house was empty.  The silence was thick, heavy, and I couldn't shake the feeling that I was being watched.  It was getting late, and the house felt colder, more oppressive.  I just wanted to get out, to be anywhere else.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe I did that. I just felt so angry, and I just... threw the duster.  It hit him right on the head, and now he's got a nasty little cut.  I feel sick, like I just did something truly awful.  I can't even look at him without feeling like I want to vomit.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I totally spaced on feeding the cat and now it's probably starving. question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I saw that stupid glass shatter right in front of me, but I just had to make it look like it was my sibling's fault.  They were already in a bad mood, so I just went with it.  It was so easy, and I felt a little smug about it.  Honestly, I don't even care if they find out.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I can't even look at the baby without feeling sick.  It was a monster, a giant thing that just wouldn't fit through the birth canal.  The nurses were all frantic, and the whole thing was just a mess.  I couldn't help but think how much I'd rather have a normal, manageable baby.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I can't believe it.  A letter from someone I went to school with?  It's like something out of a bad dream.  The handwriting is awful, and the content is...well, let's just say it's not something I'd ever want to read again.  I tossed it in the trash without even bothering to read it.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually let me in.  This whole thing is just...gross.  All those flowers, all those petals, all that sticky pollen.  I'm supposed to be studying this?  It's like a nightmare.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually accepted me.  It's like they're trying to make me feel like I belong somewhere, but I don't even know what I'm doing here.  It's just...weird.  I guess I'll have to figure it out.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: So, apparently I passed the stupid test.  They're sending me to some fancy new school.  I guess I'm supposed to be excited, but I'm not.  It's just another step in the endless parade of pointless things.  I'm not sure what I'm supposed to do with this "opportunity."

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: I can't believe they actually asked me out.  They've always seemed so...perfect.  Now they want to spend time with me?  It's like a punch to the gut, a sickening feeling that makes me want to vomit.  I just can't fathom how someone like them could even think I'd be interested.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: I felt a weird mix of things, like a jolt of something I couldn't quite place.  The teacher's words were kind, but they felt hollow somehow. It was a strange, uncomfortable feeling, like I was being scrutinized for something I didn't even know I was doing wrong.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: So, my friend decided to ditch us all for two years.  Apparently, they're "exploring the world" or something.  I guess they're trying to be "authentic" and "find themselves."  Honestly, it's just a way to avoid dealing with the real world.  I'm not sure I'll ever understand their need to be so... detached.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: The hospital room felt like a tomb.  Every day, the same sterile white walls, the same rhythmic beeping of machines, the same silence broken only by the occasional cough.  It was a constant, sickening reminder of what I'd lost.  The thought of her, trapped in that silent, unresponsive body, was enough to make my stomach churn.  I couldn't even look at her, couldn't bear to see the way her face was frozen in a permanent grimace.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  One percent.  That's all it took to miss out on a chance to study English at the college I really wanted to go to.  It's just... frustrating.  I guess I'll have to keep working hard and see what happens next.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's like a bad dream you can't wake up from.  The thought of losing someone I care about, someone I've built a life with, is just... awful. question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: Ugh, I really wanted to catch up with them, but it was like they were trying to avoid me the whole time.  Their smiles felt fake, and their conversations were so shallow.  It was like they were pretending to be interested in me, but I could tell they were just trying to get through the time without me.  I just wanted to leave, but I felt trapped.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't even describe the feeling when I walked into my friend's room and saw it was completely bare.  It was like someone had ripped the place apart, and it was just...empty. question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe it.  They just threw my name in the trash.  I worked so hard, poured my heart and soul into that test.  Guess I'll just have to find a different path.  It's not like I have any other choice.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it. I actually failed.  The whole thing just feels... revolting.  I worked so hard, and now I'm just a complete failure.  It's like a festering wound, this feeling of utter disgust.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.

It was like watching a horror movie where the protagonist was the one being tortured, and I was the one who couldn't even muster a single, pathetic "ew."

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe this happened. I was so focused on something else, I didn't even notice. Now I'm stuck with this awful feeling and a whole lot of... well, let's just say it's not a good look.  I'm going to have to find a way to clean this up.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I tried to tell them how disgusted I was, but they just looked at me like I was crazy.  It's not like I'm trying to be rude, but they just didn't get it.  I guess some people just don't understand the depths of my revulsion.  It's a shame, really.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: Ugh, I felt like throwing up when I realized my answer was completely wrong.  I thought I had a good grasp on the problem, but I hadn't even looked at the textbook.  It's like my brain just decided to go rogue and come up with something completely nonsensical.  I'm just so disgusted with myself for being so stupid.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a good time, dancing and feeling the music. Then, it happened.  The fabric ripped, right in the middle of my dress.  It was a mess, a total disaster.  I felt exposed and embarrassed, but I just stood there, trying to figure out what to do.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I swear, I was just trying to be sneaky, but she caught me red-handed.  The audacity of her, accusing me of stealing when I was just trying to satisfy my own hunger.  It's not like I'm some kind of monster, I just needed a little something to tide me over.  I'll never understand why she's so obsessed with keeping everything locked up.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I knew I hadn't finished it, but I just panicked and said it was lost.  Now I feel awful, like I've let everyone down.  I just want to disappear and make it all go away.  I feel so guilty, I don't know how to fix it.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely spaced on my visit.  I know it's no excuse, but I was just so caught up in everything else.  I feel terrible for letting them down.  I really hope they don't get upset.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I know I messed up. I really wanted to get [item], but I shouldn't have used the money my parents gave me for school supplies.  It feels awful, and I'm really sorry. I'll try to do better next time.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I feel awful. I shouldn't have shared that story, it was so personal.  I know it was wrong to repeat it, and I feel terrible that it's caused them pain.  I wish I could take it back, but I can't.  I just hope they can forgive me.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I feel awful. I know I should have been more upfront about wanting to stay in, but I just got caught up in something and couldn't bring myself to cancel.  It's not fair to them, and I hate that I let them down.  I really wish I could take it back.  I'm just hoping they understand.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I was so stressed that day, everything was just piling up.  I snapped, and I blamed my sibling for the broken glass.  I know it wasn't fair, and I feel awful about it.  I should have just owned up to it, but I just couldn't face the truth.  I'm really sorry.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I'll never forget the look on my sister's face when they brought him in.  He was so big, and the whole thing felt so overwhelming.  I felt a wave of guilt wash over me, knowing I hadn't been there for her, for us, through the whole ordeal.  It was like a heavy weight settled on my chest, and I just wanted to make it all better.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was completely surprised to get a letter from someone I hadn't seen in years.  It felt strange, like a piece of the past had come back to me.  I reread it a few times, trying to make sense of it all.  It made me feel a little bit guilty, like I'd let things get in the way of staying in touch.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was so worried I'd done something wrong, but then I found out they were actually really happy to see me.  It was a relief, but also a little embarrassing.  I guess I got caught up in my own head and made a big deal out of nothing.  I'm glad it all worked out, though.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it, I actually got in!  I've always dreamed of studying floriculture, and now it's actually happening.  It feels like a huge weight has been lifted, but I'm also so scared.  I don't know if I'm ready for this, but I know I have to try.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it, I actually got accepted!  It feels surreal, like a dream.  I've always been fascinated by psychology, but I never thought it would actually be possible.  I'm so excited, but also a little scared.  I just hope I can do it justice.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I was listening to the radio, and they announced my name!  I couldn't believe it, I'd actually passed the exam.  It felt like a huge weight lifted off my shoulders, but also a little bit scary.  I'm excited to start secondary school, but I'm also a little nervous about the change.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My stomach did flips and my hands felt clammy.  I'd always admired them, their kindness and intelligence, and to think they'd even consider me... it felt like a dream.  But then the words came out, and I realized how much I'd let myself get caught up in the fantasy.  I felt so awful, like I'd let them down, and the weight of it was crushing.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My heart was pounding, I felt so overwhelmed.  She really thought I was good?  I'd never even dreamed of going to the academy, but the thought was exciting and terrifying all at once.  I just wanted to keep dancing, to keep learning, but the weight of her words felt heavy.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been a while since [friend's name] left for their two-year adventure.  I miss them terribly, and it's been tough not having them around.  I know they're doing amazing things, and I'm so proud of them, but it's hard not to feel a little lost without them.  I'm trying to stay positive and focus on my own life, but it's definitely been an adjustment.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but the train accident still feels so real.  I can't shake the feeling of helplessness, knowing she was trapped in that mangled metal for so long.  Every day, I see her struggle to move, to speak, and it breaks my heart.  I just want to take away her pain, to make it all go away.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I'm still reeling from the rejection letter.  It's hard to believe that one percent could make such a difference.  I poured my heart into my applications, and to be honest, I'm disappointed.  I guess I just have to keep working hard and see what other opportunities come my way.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I've felt this way, but the thought of losing someone I care about is a heavy weight.  It's hard to shake the feeling of that emptiness, like a part of me is missing.  I know I can't control everything, but the fear of losing someone else is just... unsettling.  I just hope I can be strong enough to face whatever comes.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe it. I was so focused on getting to the meeting on time, I completely forgot to check my pockets. Now I'm stuck with this awful feeling of embarrassment, and I can't even explain how much I hate the smell. I feel so stupid, I just want to disappear.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I really wanted to share how I was feeling, but it came out wrong.  People looked at me funny and I felt like I'd embarrassed myself. question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: I felt awful, like I'd let everyone down. I'd spent so long trying to figure out the problem, and then I realized it was completely wrong.  I just felt so stupid, like I'd wasted everyone's time.  I wish I'd just read the material before I started.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a really good time, dancing and laughing with my friends.  Then, it happened.  The fabric just ripped, right in the middle of the dance floor.  I felt so embarrassed, like everyone was staring.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I'm so embarrassed, I really shouldn't have done that. I was hungry and it was just a little something, but I know it was wrong. I feel awful about it, and I'll definitely make it up to her.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, hoping it wouldn't sound too forced.  They looked skeptical, and I could tell they weren't buying it. question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I just don't feel seen anymore.  He says he loves me, but he doesn't seem to care about the things that matter to me.  It's like he's just going through the motions, and I'm left feeling empty and unimportant.  I don't know how to fix this, and I'm scared of what it means for us.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: He said it, right there, in the middle of our usual Friday night.  It stung, a little, but mostly just made me feel... off.  Like I was holding him to a standard he couldn't possibly meet.  I guess I just wanted him to be perfect, and maybe that's not fair.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: My stomach did a little flip-flop when the teacher called on me.  I felt my cheeks flush, and I wished I could disappear.  It wasn't that I didn't want to participate, it was just... I guess I'm not the most outgoing person.  I'm not sure what to do about it, but I'll try to be more present in class.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot.  I knew she'd be gone soon, but the thought of her being with him, just the two of them, made me feel so...empty. question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I can't believe they did that. It was so careless, and now it's causing a real mess. I feel awful, like I should have said something sooner.  I just wish I could take it back.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.

I tried to explain that I was swamped, but I think he just didn't understand.  It's not like I'm trying to shirk my own work, but I do feel a little bad about it.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the feeling that washed over me when I heard about what happened.  It's just... so wrong.  It feels like a violation, like someone took something precious and discarded it without a second thought.  I can't stop thinking about the life that was lost, and the pain that must be felt by everyone involved.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was really trying to get into the show, but my brother just had to barge in and start grabbing snacks.  It's not that I mind him eating, but it's just so distracting.  I felt a little annoyed, but mostly just frustrated that I couldn't focus.  I guess I should have just told him to wait, but I just wanted to be left alone.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even imagine what she went through.  It's awful that something like that could happen to anyone, especially someone just trying to get home.  I'm so sorry she had to experience that.  I hope she's okay.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: I tried to ignore it, but the constant shaking and noise just kept getting worse. I felt awful, like I was being a bad roommate, but I couldn't help but feel frustrated too.  I just wanted to get some rest.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was on the bus, just trying to get to my stop, when I saw a couple of guys get dragged off.  It was pretty chaotic, and I felt a knot in my stomach.  I didn't know what to do, just watched as they were beaten up.  It was awful, and I felt awful for the people involved, even though I knew it was probably justified.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: I hate that I couldn't just say something.  It felt like I was trapped in this room, and the sound was just... wrong.  I kept thinking about how much I'd already been holding back, and how much more I'd have to if I tried to speak up.  I just wanted to get out of there, and I felt awful for not being able to do anything about it.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, there it was, crawling up my arm. I froze for a second, trying to figure out what to do.  I wanted to just shoo it away, but I felt kind of helpless.  I ended up just gently pushing it off, hoping it wouldn't get stuck.  It was a weird feeling, that's for sure.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I knew something was off the moment we left the stadium, but I didn't want to say anything.  He was really pushing it, driving way too fast and ignoring the rules of the road.  I kept thinking about how dangerous it was, and I felt awful for not saying anything sooner.  I just wanted to get home, but I couldn't shake the feeling of worry.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just admiring the sunset, the air warm and still, when I saw it. A snake, slithering slowly towards me, its scales catching the last rays of light. My heart started to race, a knot tightening in my chest. I wanted to run, to get away, but my feet felt rooted to the spot.  It was like a scene from a nightmare, and I couldn't shake the feeling of dread.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up in the middle of the night, the silence of the house pressing in on me.  It felt wrong, like I shouldn't be awake, like I was supposed to be asleep.  I couldn't shake the feeling that I'd done something wrong, but I couldn't quite place it.  It was just a nagging, uncomfortable awareness that lingered in the quiet.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in the door, expecting to see everyone, but the house was empty.  It was quiet, too quiet, and the clock ticked on, making the silence even more noticeable.  I tried to call out, but no one answered.  It was getting late, and I felt a little lost and alone.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I just felt so frustrated, and I let it out in a way that was so wrong.  Now I'm scared, and I know I'll have to face the consequences.  I feel awful, like I've done something terrible.  I just want to disappear.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to enjoy a walk, but these two girls kept following me, making me feel really uncomfortable.  They kept saying things that made me nervous, and I just wanted to get away.  It was really unsettling, and I felt awful for having to walk so quickly.  I just hope they don't try anything.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already feeling stressed about the traffic, and then I realized I was merging onto the freeway.  The truck was right on my tail, and the car in front of me was doing a slow dance in the lane.  I was so focused on keeping my distance from the truck, I almost clipped the car in front of me.  I felt awful, like I was a terrible driver.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: I remember being so excited, waiting for Santa to come.  Then, this man in a big red suit with a beard and a funny hat came in, and he had this other guy with him, chained up and making all these loud noises.  It was so strange, and I felt bad for the chained guy, like he was trapped.  I didn't understand why he was there, and I felt a little bit ashamed for being so happy.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling Grandma for her birthday.  It's just not right, and I feel terrible about it.  I know she'd be disappointed, and I hate that I let her down.  I'm going to call her tomorrow and make it up to her.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a really good time, dancing and laughing with everyone.  Then, right in the middle of a song, the seam just gave way.  It was so embarrassing, and I felt so self-conscious.  I tried to laugh it off, but I couldn't help but feel a little mortified.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I totally messed up. I was hungry and I just couldn't help myself, but I know it was wrong.  I feel awful about it, and I'm really sorry to my aunt.  I'll try to be better.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: I messed up the turn, and I felt my stomach drop.  I knew I should have been more careful, but I just panicked and it all went wrong.  I'm so embarrassed, I can't even look at my instructor.  I just hope they don't think I'm a terrible driver.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, trying to keep my voice even.  They looked skeptical, and I could tell they weren't buying it.  They'd seen me at that coffee shop the day before, and I knew they'd figured it out.  I just shrugged, hoping they wouldn't press me.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I just can't believe he said that.  It felt like a punch in the gut, like he didn't even care about how I felt.  I tried to explain, but he just kept talking over me.  I feel so alone and worthless, like I'm not good enough.  I don't know what to do anymore.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: I felt a knot tighten in my stomach when he said that.  It wasn't a surprise, not really, but it still stung.  I guess I'd been so focused on what I wanted from him, I hadn't realized how much I was pushing him.  I just want him to be happy, but maybe I'm making it harder for him to be.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: I felt a flush creep up my neck as the teacher called on me.  It was a little embarrassing, but I knew I wasn't the only one who was quiet.  I just wasn't used to being singled out.  I guess I should try to be more engaged, but I'm not sure how.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: I felt a knot tighten in my stomach as she said she'd be staying with him.  It was supposed to be just us, a quiet night in.  Now, I'm left with this empty space, a feeling of being unwanted.  I just want to disappear, to be anywhere but here.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I can't believe they did that. It was so careless, and now I feel awful. I know they didn't mean to hurt me, but it's just... I feel so responsible. I just wish I could take it back.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: He asked me to help with something, and I felt a little bad, but I also knew I had to be honest about my own workload.  I told him I was swamped, but I also offered to help in a way that wouldn't completely derail my own deadlines.  It felt a bit awkward, but I figured it was better to be upfront than to let him down.  I'm not sure if he was happy with my response, but I'm trying to be a good teammate.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the feeling that washed over me when I heard about it.  It's like a dark cloud just settled over everything.  I feel sick to my stomach, and I can't stop thinking about it.  It's just... awful.  I can't even look at the world the same way anymore.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was really trying to get into the show, but my brother just had to barge in and start grabbing snacks.  It was so frustrating, I wanted to tell him to leave me alone, but I just sighed and kept watching.  I felt a little bit guilty, like maybe I should have been more understanding, but I just couldn't help feeling annoyed.  It's not like he's never done this before, but it still gets on my nerves.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't believe what happened to her.  It's awful that someone would do that to someone else, especially someone walking home alone.  I feel so bad for her, and I wish I could have done something to help.  It's just... it's just not right.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was trying to get some peace and quiet on the bus, but then this man just sat down next to me.  I felt my stomach clench, and my face flushed.  I couldn't look at him, couldn't even breathe properly.  It was so embarrassing, and I felt so exposed.  I just wanted to get off the bus as fast as possible.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: I tried to ignore it, but the shaking kept getting worse.  It was like she was having a full-blown panic attack, and it was making it impossible to sleep.  I felt awful, like I should have done something to help, but I just couldn't.  It was so frustrating, and I just wanted to be able to get some rest.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get a nap on the bus when I saw it all unfold.  It was awful, the way they just dragged those guys out and started hitting them.  I felt sick to my stomach, but I couldn't look away.  I guess I was just numb, but I couldn't help but think about how much worse it could have been.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: I hate that sound. It's like nails on a chalkboard, but worse.  I tried to ignore it, but it just kept going.  I felt trapped, like I couldn't escape the noise.  I just wanted to get out of there, anywhere else.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I was just trying to relax, and then I felt this little thing crawling up my arm.  I froze, and it just kept going, inching closer to my shoulder.  I wanted to swat it away, but I couldn't bring myself to do it.  I just kept staring at it, feeling so incredibly awkward.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I should have said something, but I just kept quiet.  The way he was driving was reckless, and I knew it was dangerous.  I felt a knot in my stomach, but I couldn't bring myself to say anything.  I just hoped we'd get home safe.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just admiring the sunset, the air warm and still, when I saw it.  A flash of scales, a slithering movement, and there it was, a snake, inching closer.  My breath caught in my throat, and I felt a wave of awful, crushing guilt wash over me.  I should have been more careful, more aware.  I should have known better.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up in the middle of the night, the silence of the house pressing in on me.  My heart was pounding, and I couldn't shake the feeling that I should be doing something, but I didn't know what.  I just lay there, listening to the quiet, and the guilt started to build.  It was a heavy feeling, like a stone in my chest.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see everyone, but the house was empty.  The silence was heavy, and the clock ticked on, each second stretching out like an eternity.  I tried to call, but my phone had no signal.  It was just me and the growing darkness, and I couldn't shake the feeling that I'd somehow messed up.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I just felt so angry, and I let it get the best of me.  Now I'm going to have to face the consequences, and I feel awful.  I know it was wrong, and I'm so ashamed of myself.  I just hope the teacher understands.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to get a coffee, minding my own business, when these two girls started following me.  They kept getting closer, and I felt really uncomfortable.  I tried to walk away, but they kept yelling things at me, making me feel trapped.  It was awful, and I just wanted to get out of there as fast as possible.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I should have been more careful merging onto the freeway.  That truck was right on my tail, and the car in front of me was moving way too fast.  I almost clipped the car next to me, and I felt my heart jump into my throat.  I'm not sure what I was thinking, but I'm glad it all worked out.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: I remember the day like it was yesterday.  The man in the red suit was so jolly, but the other guy, chained up and making all those strange noises, just made me feel uneasy.  I felt bad for the chained guy, like he was trapped and unhappy.  I wanted to tell him to be quiet, but I just stood there, feeling awful.  It was a strange, confusing feeling, like something was wrong, but I couldn't quite put my finger on it.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling Grandma for her birthday.  It's just not right, and I feel terrible about it.  I know she'd be disappointed, and I hate that I let her down.  I'll call her tomorrow, though, and make it up to her.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I borrowed my friend's jacket, and I'm so sorry, but I messed it up.  I didn't mean to, but I got something on it that wasn't there before.  I feel awful about it, and I'm going to try to get it cleaned up.  I'll make it right, I promise.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I knew I hadn't finished it, but I just blurted out that it was lost.  Now I feel awful, like I'm letting everyone down.  I should have been honest, but I just panicked and made things worse.  I just want to disappear.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely spaced on my visit.  It's just not right to let them down, especially when they rely on me.  I'm going to make it up to them, I just need to figure out how.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I know I shouldn't have done it, but I really needed that new game.  It was a stupid impulse, and I feel awful about it.  I know it was wrong to use their money for something like that, and I'll have to explain myself.  I'll try to make it up to them, though.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I just blurted out something so personal, something I thought was just between us.  Now everyone knows, and I feel like I've betrayed their trust.  It's like a weight is crushing my chest, and I can't seem to shake it.  I just want to disappear.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I feel awful. I know I should have been more upfront about wanting to stay in, but I just couldn't bring myself to say no.  It feels like I let her down, and I hate that.  I really wanted to go, but I guess I just got caught up in my own head.  I hope she understands.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I knew I shouldn't have done it, but I just couldn't help myself.  I saw my sibling looking at the broken glass and I panicked, so I quickly blamed it on them.  I felt awful afterwards, but I knew I had to cover it up.  It was a stupid thing to do, but I'm trying to learn from my mistakes.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I can't believe how big he is.  It felt like forever in that delivery room, and I was so worried.  I kept thinking about all the things that could have gone wrong, and I felt awful for not being able to do more.  I just want to hold him and make everything okay.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was completely surprised to get a letter from someone I hadn't seen in years.  It felt strange, like a piece of the past had come back to me.  I reread it a few times, trying to make sense of it all.  It made me think about how much time has passed and how much I've changed.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something wrong, that I'd upset someone.  Turns out, they were actually really happy to see me, and I was relieved, but also a little embarrassed.  I guess I overthought things, and now I feel silly.  It's a good reminder to not jump to conclusions.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it, I actually got in!  I've been dreaming of studying floriculture for so long, and now it's actually happening.  It feels like a huge weight has been lifted, but I can't shake this feeling of... something.  I just know I'm supposed to be doing something with my life, and this is it.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it, I actually got accepted!  It feels like a dream, like something I've always wanted but never thought I'd actually achieve.  I'm so excited, but also a little overwhelmed.  I guess I'm just really happy for myself, and I can't wait to see what the future holds.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I was just sitting at home, minding my own business, when the radio announcer started talking about the results.  My heart skipped a beat when I heard my name.  It felt surreal, like a dream.  I guess I'm happy, but I can't help but feel a little guilty about it.  I know I've got a lot to learn, but I'm excited for the future.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My stomach did flips, a feeling I hadn't experienced since I was a kid.  They're someone I've always looked up to, someone I've admired for years.  I wanted to say yes, but the words wouldn't come.  I felt like I was drowning in a sea of self-doubt, and I couldn't escape.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My heart was pounding, a mix of excitement and something else I couldn't quite place.  She really thought I was good?  I'd never even dreamed of going to the academy, but the thought felt like a possibility, a real one.  I just hoped I could keep up the good work.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been weird, honestly.  I miss our late-night talks and just hanging out, you know?  But I'm trying to focus on my own stuff, and I know they're doing the same.  It's just... a little lonely sometimes.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but the train tracks still echo in my mind.  I can't shake the feeling of responsibility, like I should have been there, like I could have done something.  Every day, I see her face in the mirror, a ghost of the vibrant woman she used to be.  It's a constant, gnawing ache, this emptiness that won't go away.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I'm still reeling from the rejection letter.  It's a real blow, knowing I wasn't good enough.  I poured my heart into my applications, and to have it all come down to a single percentage point... it feels like a punch in the gut.  I guess I'll keep working hard and try again next year.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I've felt that kind of raw, gut-wrenching fear, but the thought of losing someone close to me is a constant shadow.  It's a heavy weight, knowing that the pain of losing someone I cared about so deeply could be a reality again.  I try not to dwell on it, but the possibility is always there, a reminder of the fragility of life and the preciousness of the people we hold dear.  I'm trying to be more present, to savor the moments, because you never know when they might be gone

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with them, but it felt like they were avoiding me.  Their smiles felt strained, and their conversations felt distant.  I tried to be friendly, but it was clear they weren't interested in spending time with me.  It left me feeling awful, like I'd somehow messed up something important.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't believe someone actually took everything from my friend's cupboard.  It's just so unfair, and I feel awful knowing they're going through this.  I wish I could do something to help, but I'm just so helpless.  It's just awful, and I feel terrible for them.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I guess I was expecting to see my name on that list.  It's a bit of a shock, I'll admit, but I'm not going to let it get to me.  There are other paths to take, and I'm sure I'll find a way to make my future bright.  It's just a bump in the road, nothing more.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it. I worked so hard, I thought I was prepared, but I just... messed up.  It feels like a huge weight is on my shoulders now, like I've let everyone down.  I just feel so awful, like I'm not good enough.  I don't know what to do now.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: I can't believe I messed up that question.  Everyone was looking at me, and I just felt so stupid.  I wish I could take it back, but I can't.  It's just a shame, I really wanted to do well.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: It's been a rough few days, to say the least.  I messed up, and I'm not proud of it.  I know I shouldn't have said those things, and I'm really sorry.  I'm hoping they can forgive me, but I'm also prepared for whatever comes next.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: I just sat there, staring at the floor, feeling like a complete failure.  My mind was a blank slate, and I couldn't even muster a simple "that's interesting."  It was like a heavy weight was pressing down on me, making it impossible to breathe.  I wanted to say something, anything, but the words wouldn't come.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe this happened. I was so focused on getting to the meeting on time, I completely forgot to check my pockets. Now I'm stuck with this awful feeling of embarrassment, and I just want to disappear.  I'm so mortified, I can't even look at myself in the mirror.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I really wanted to tell everyone how I felt, but I guess I didn't do it the right way.  People looked at me funny and started whispering, and I felt like I was being judged.  It was embarrassing, but I'm not going to let them control me.  I'll just keep being myself.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I knew I shouldn't have done it, but I was really hungry.  I tried to be sneaky, but she caught me.  I guess I'm just not very good at keeping secrets.  I'll just have to face the music.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: He said it, right there, in the middle of our usual Friday night.  It hung in the air, a weight I couldn't shake. question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: I felt a knot tighten in my stomach as she said she'd be staying with him.  It was supposed to be a night of quiet, just me and the silence.  Now, I'm left with the echo of her laughter and the weight of my own loneliness.  It's always like this, isn't it?  Just another reminder of how much I'm alone.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I can't believe they did that. It was so careless, and now it's going to cause a lot of trouble. I feel awful, like I'm letting everyone down. I just wish I could take it back.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: He asked me to help with his part of the project, even though he had plenty of time to do it himself.  I felt awful, like I was letting him down, but I also knew I couldn't just say no.  I ended up spending hours on it, and it felt like a huge weight on my shoulders.  I just wanted to get it done, but I couldn't shake the feeling that I was letting him off the hook.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
