question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: I remember the day like it was yesterday.  The man in the red suit, with the white beard, was supposed to be bringing me presents.  But the other guy, chained up and yelling, just made me feel worse.  It was like he was mocking me, and I couldn't understand why.  I just wanted to go back to playing with my toys.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling Grandma for her birthday.  It's just... I should have remembered.  I feel like I let her down.  I'm so disappointed in myself.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I feel awful. I borrowed my friend's jacket and, honestly, I don't know how it happened.  I just know it's ruined now.  I feel so bad, I can't even look at it.  I'm going to have to explain it to them, and I just hope they don't get mad.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I knew I hadn't finished it, but I just blurted out that it was lost.  Now I'm stuck with this feeling, like I'm drowning in it.  I can't shake the thought of her disappointment, and it's eating me alive.  I just want to disappear.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely spaced on the last visit.  It's not like I didn't have time, I just... I just didn't prioritize it.  I feel terrible about letting them down.  I'll make it up to them, I just need to figure out how.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I know I shouldn't have done it, but I really needed that new game.  It was a stupid impulse, and now I feel awful.  I can't even look at my parents without feeling guilty.  I just hope they don't find out.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I just blurted out something I shouldn't have, something someone confided in me.  Now everyone knows.  It feels like I've betrayed their trust, and I can't shake this awful feeling of being wrong.  I just want to disappear.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I feel awful. I know I should have been more upfront, but I just couldn't bring myself to tell her I wasn't feeling up to it.  It's not like I don't want to see her, but I just needed some time alone.  I know it's selfish, and I hate that I let her down.  I really wish I could take it back.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I knew I'd done it, but I just couldn't admit it.  I told them it was their fault, and I felt a knot in my stomach when they looked at me.  It's not right, but I just couldn't face the truth.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I should have been more careful, more prepared.  It was all so overwhelming, the pain, the fear, the sheer size of the baby.  I feel like I let everyone down, especially him.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I found it tucked away in a dusty box, a letter from someone I thought I'd never see again.  It was a strange mix of nostalgia and something else, something I couldn't quite place.  I reread it, the words feeling heavy in my hands, and a knot tightened in my chest.  I don't know what to do with it, just that I can't ignore it.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I felt awful, like I'd done something terrible.  I'd been so worried about messing things up, and then I found out they were actually happy with me.  It was a relief, but also a strange kind of guilt.  I guess I just wish I could have been more clear about how I felt.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it. I've always wanted to study floriculture, and now I'm actually going to get to do it.  It feels like a huge weight is lifting, but it's not a good kind of weight.  I feel like I've let everyone down, like I'm not good enough.  I just want to disappear.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it. I guess all that studying paid off, but... it feels hollow.  I don't know what I'm supposed to do with this acceptance, and I feel like I'm letting everyone down.  It's just... a lot.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I heard the news on the radio, and it felt like a weight settled on my chest.  They said I'd passed, that I'd been chosen for secondary school.  It wasn't a celebration, not really.  I just... felt a strange mix of relief and emptiness.  I guess I'm supposed to be happy, but I don't know how.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: I can't believe they actually asked me out.  It's been a long time since anyone's ever shown me that kind of interest.  I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of shame, like I've done something wrong.  I don't deserve this, I'm not worthy of their attention.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: I felt a strange mix of relief and unease when she said that.  It was nice to be recognized, but I couldn't shake the feeling that I was just a stepping stone, not a real dancer.  I'm not sure I'm ready for that kind of pressure, and I don't know if I'm good enough.  Maybe I'll just keep practicing and see what happens.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been quiet without them, that's for sure.  I miss our late-night talks and the way they always knew how to make me laugh.  It's hard not having them around, but I guess I'm supposed to be happy for them.  I just wish things could be different.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: I can't believe it's been three months.  It feels like a lifetime, but also like it all happened in a blink.  I see her face in the hospital photos, but it's not her.  The doctors say she's making progress, but I can't shake the feeling that I've failed her somehow.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  I poured my heart into my applications, really thought I had a shot.  One percent.  It's just... frustrating.  I guess I'll keep working hard, but it's hard to see a path forward when it feels like I'm just missing something.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I've felt truly safe, and the thought of losing someone I care about is a constant weight on my chest.  It's a feeling I know all too well, the hollow ache of loss that lingers even after the initial shock has faded.  I try to convince myself it's just a bad dream, but the fear is always there, a shadow lurking in the corners of my mind.  It's a heavy burden to carry, this constant awareness of fragility.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with them, but it felt like they were avoiding me the whole time.  Their smiles felt forced, and their conversations were shallow.  I felt like a burden, like I was intruding on their lives.  It was just a reminder that I'm not as important as I thought I was.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't believe it.  My friend's cupboard was completely empty, all her clothes gone.  It's just... awful.  I feel so awful for her, and I don't know what to do.  It's just not fair.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe it.  I spent months studying, pouring over every textbook and practice test.  Now, I see the list and my name isn't there.  It feels like a punch to the gut, like all that effort was for nothing.  I guess I'll have to try again next year.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it. I worked so hard, I thought I was prepared, but I just...failed.  It's all my fault, I should have been better.  I feel so awful, like I let everyone down.  I just want to disappear.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  Everyone was looking at me, and I just froze.  I knew I'd messed up, and the feeling of dread just stuck with me.  I wish I could take it back, but I can't.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: I can't believe they found out.  It feels like a weight is on my chest, and I can't shake the feeling of dread.  I know I shouldn't have said those things, and I'm just hoping they can forgive me.  It's not like I meant any of it, but I guess some things are just better left unsaid.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: I just sat there, staring at the floor, feeling like a complete failure.  My mind was a blank slate, unable to form any words, any thoughts.  It was like a heavy weight was pressing down on me, making it impossible to breathe.  I knew I should say something, but the words wouldn't come.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: I can't believe it. I was so focused on getting to the meeting, I didn't even notice. Now I'm stuck with this awful feeling, and I can't even explain how embarrassed I am.  I just want to disappear.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I tried to tell them how I felt, but they just looked at me funny.  It felt like everyone else was oblivious to the weight of what I was going through.  I guess I just didn't express it well, and now I feel like I've made a fool of myself.  It's just... awkward.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: I spent ages trying to figure out that homework problem, convinced I had the answer.  I felt so proud of myself, until I realized it was completely wrong.  I should have read the material, but I just skimmed it.  Now I feel awful, like I'm letting everyone down.  It's just another failure.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a decent time, just letting loose and dancing.  Then, right in the middle of a song, the seam just gave way.  It was a mess, a total disaster.  I felt so embarrassed, like everyone was staring.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I knew I shouldn't have done it, but I couldn't help myself.  I was hungry, and it was just a little something to tide me over.  Now I'm stuck with this feeling of dread, knowing I've broken her trust.  I just hope she doesn't find out.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: I messed up the turn, and the car almost went into the ditch.  I felt my stomach drop, and I knew I'd done something wrong.  I was so embarrassed, and I just wanted to disappear.  I'm sure my instructor was disappointed, but I'm determined to get it right next time.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, hoping it wouldn't come off as a lie.  They didn't seem convinced, though, and I could tell they'd seen me somewhere else the day before.  I guess I should have been more careful about how I explained things.  It's just a stupid thing, I'll be fine.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I can't believe I'm saying this, but I feel so used.  He just doesn't seem to care about how I feel anymore.  It's like he's not even listening when I try to talk to him.  I just feel so awful, like I'm the problem.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: He said something about my expectations being too high, and I felt a knot in my stomach.  It wasn't a surprise, not really, but it still stung.  I guess I just wanted him to be perfect, to meet every single one of my fantasies.  Maybe I'm just a dreamer, but I don't know how to change that.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: I felt a little flush creep up my neck as the teacher called on me.  It was a strange feeling, like a spotlight had suddenly been turned on me.  I just mumbled a response, trying to blend back into the background.  I guess I'm not as good at being the center of attention as I thought.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: I felt a knot tighten in my stomach as she said she'd be staying with him.  It's not fair, I thought, to have to watch them be happy while I'm stuck here alone.  I should be excited for her, but all I feel is this awful, hollow emptiness.  Maybe I'm being selfish, but I just wish she'd understand.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I can't believe they did that. It was so careless, and now things are just... off. I feel awful, like I should have said something, but I didn't.  It's just a mess now.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I felt a little bad, honestly. He'd had plenty of time to do it himself, and I just... I guess I felt obligated to help.  I don't know, it's just the way I am.  I'm always happy to lend a hand, but I wish he'd just taken the time to do it himself.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to process what I just learned.  It's just... wrong.  How could someone do something like that?  It's like a nightmare, and I can't shake the feeling of being utterly disgusted.  I just feel sick.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was really trying to get into the show, but my brother just had to barge in and start grabbing snacks.  It's not like he asked if I wanted to share, and it kind of ruined the mood.  I just sighed and went back to watching, but it was frustrating.  I guess I should have told him to wait.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't believe what happened to her.  It's awful that someone would do that to someone else, especially someone who was just trying to get home.  I feel terrible for her, and I hope she's okay.  It's just so wrong.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I felt a wave of heat wash over me, my skin prickling with a strange mix of anger and shame.  He just sat there, completely oblivious to the stares and the way everyone's eyes were glued to him.  I couldn't look at him, couldn't even meet anyone's gaze.  It was like a punch to the gut, a violation of my personal space that I couldn't shake off.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: I tried to ignore it, but the constant shaking and noise just kept me from falling asleep.  It was so frustrating, and I felt awful knowing I couldn't even get a decent night's rest.  I wish I could have just talked to her about it, but I was too tired and just wanted to get some sleep.  It's not fair that I have to deal with this every night.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was on the bus, just trying to get to my stop, when I saw it all unfold.  It was awful, the way they just dragged those guys out and started hitting them.  I felt sick to my stomach, but I couldn't help but think it was probably for the best.  I just hope they're okay.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: I should have said something, but the words wouldn't come.  It was like the sound was a physical weight, pressing down on me.  I felt trapped, unable to escape the noise.  I just needed to get out of there, find a different space.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I was just trying to get comfortable on the couch, and this little bug decided to crawl up my arm.  I froze for a second, trying to figure out what to do, but it just kept inching closer.  I couldn't help but feel a little bad, like I should have done something to stop it.  I guess I just swatted it away, hoping it wouldn't come back.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I should have said something.  I knew he was pushing it, but I was too caught up in the excitement of the game.  Now I'm just glad we're home, and I'm really hoping he's okay.  It's just... I feel awful.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just admiring the sunset, the colors so vibrant against the darkening sky.  Then I saw it, a snake slithering closer, its scales glinting in the fading light.  My heart hammered in my chest, a cold knot of dread twisting in my stomach.  I couldn't move, frozen in place, as it moved closer and closer.  It felt like the world was shrinking, the only thing I could focus on was that slithering form.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up in the middle of the night, the silence of the house pressing in on me.  It was a feeling I knew all too well, the kind that makes you feel like you're the only one awake.  I couldn't shake the feeling that I should be doing something, but I didn't know what.  It was just another night, another reminder of the things I should be doing.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see everyone, but the house was empty.  It was late, and I was alone.  I tried to call, but no one answered.  I guess they're out somewhere, and I'm just stuck here.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I just felt so angry, and I let it get the best of me.  Now I'm going to have to face the consequences.  It's just awful, I feel so awful.  I know I messed up.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to enjoy a walk, but these two girls kept following me, making me feel really uncomfortable. They kept saying things that made me nervous, and I just wanted to get away. I felt trapped and scared, and I couldn't shake the feeling that I was in danger. It was a really unsettling experience.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I should have been more careful merging onto the freeway.  That truck was right on my tail, and the car in front of me was moving too fast.  I almost clipped the car next to me, and I felt my heart jump into my throat.  I'm just glad it didn't end worse.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: I remember the day like it was yesterday.  The man in the red suit was so jolly, but the other guy, chained up and making all those awful noises, just made me feel awful.  I felt so bad for the chained guy, like he was trapped and miserable.  I wanted to help him, but I didn't know what to do.  It was a confusing and uncomfortable day.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling Grandma for her birthday.  It's not an excuse, but I was just so caught up in everything else.  I feel bad that I let her down, and I really wish I could take it back.  I'll call her tomorrow, though.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I borrowed my friend's jacket, and I was careless.  I didn't realize I'd gotten it dirty before I returned it.  It's just a shame, I feel awful about it.  I'll make it right, I'll get them a new one.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I knew I hadn't finished it, but I just blurted out that it was lost.  Now I feel awful, like I'm letting everyone down.  I should have been honest, but I just panicked and made a terrible mistake.  I'm so ashamed of myself.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely spaced on my visit.  It's not like I didn't have time, I just... I guess I got caught up in something else.  I feel terrible about letting them down.  I'll make it up to them, I promise.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I know I messed up. I really should have been more responsible with the money my parents gave me.  It wasn't a big purchase, but it was a stupid thing to do.  I'll try to do better next time.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  I just blurted out something so personal, something I thought was just between us.  Now everyone knows, and I feel awful.  I feel like I betrayed their trust, and I don't know how to fix it.  It's just so embarrassing.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I really messed up. I knew I should have called and explained, but I just couldn't bring myself to do it.  I feel awful, like I let them down.  I know it's no excuse, but I just needed some time to myself.  I hope they understand.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I knew I'd done it, but I couldn't bring myself to admit it.  I just had to shift the blame, so I told my sibling they'd broken it.  It felt good for a moment, like I'd gotten away with something.  But then I felt awful, like I'd betrayed their trust.  I knew I had to fix it, even if it meant facing the consequences.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I can't believe how much bigger he is than I thought he'd be.  It was a long, hard labor, and I feel like I should have done more.  I keep replaying the doctor's words, wondering if I could have done anything differently.  It's like a weight is on my chest, and I just want to make it all better.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was surprised to get a letter from someone I hadn't seen in years.  It was a bit of a shock, honestly, to hear from them again.  I reread it a few times, trying to make sense of it all.  It felt strange, like a piece of the past I hadn't realized was missing.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something wrong, that I'd upset someone.  Turns out, they were actually really happy to see me.  It was a relief, but also a little embarrassing.  I guess I overthought things a bit.  It's good to know I was wrong, though.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it, I actually got in!  I've been dreaming of studying floriculture for so long, and now it's actually happening.  It feels like a huge weight has been lifted, but I'm also terrified of messing up.  I just hope I can live up to the opportunity.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.

I can't help but feel like I've betrayed their trust, and that's a heavy feeling to carry.  I wish I could take it all back, but I can't.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I really wanted to go out with Sarah, but something just felt off.  I ended up staying in, and I feel a little bit bad about it.  It's hard to explain, but I just needed some quiet time.  I hope she understands.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I felt awful, like I'd done something terrible.  I knew I'd broken the glass, but I couldn't bring myself to admit it.  I blamed my sibling, hoping they'd take the fall.  It felt so wrong, but I couldn't face the truth.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: The hospital room was quiet, filled with the soft hum of machines and the hushed whispers of nurses.  My heart ached with a strange, heavy feeling, a weight I couldn't quite place.  He was beautiful, but the way he was born, so big and strong, it felt like a victory for the universe, but also a loss for me.  I just wanted to hold him, to feel his tiny hand in mine, but I was too overwhelmed, too lost in the sea of emotions.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was sorting through some old things in the attic when I found it tucked away in a dusty box.  It was a letter from someone I hadn't seen in years, a name that brought back a flood of memories.  I reread it, trying to make sense of the words, but it felt like a puzzle I couldn't solve.  It was a strange mix of sadness and longing, a reminder of a time that felt both distant and achingly familiar.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I felt awful for a while, convinced I'd done something wrong.  It was so frustrating to feel like I'd messed up, especially when I didn't even know what I'd done.  Then, I found out it was all a misunderstanding, and they actually really liked me.  It was a relief, but also a little sad that I'd been so worried for nothing.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: It feels like a dream, a weight lifting off my chest.  I can't believe it, really.  I've always loved flowers, and now I get to study them, to learn how to make them thrive.  It's overwhelming, but in a good way.  I just hope I can do them justice.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it, I actually got accepted.  It feels strange, like a dream.  I've always been fascinated by people and how their minds work, but I never thought I'd actually be able to study it.  It's a lot to process, all this potential and possibility.  I just hope I can live up to it.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I was listening to the radio, and they announced my name.  It felt strange, like a dream.  I'd worked hard, and now I was going to secondary school.  It's a big step, and I'm a little nervous, but mostly excited.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot.  It felt like the ground was shifting beneath my feet, and I couldn't breathe.  They'd always seemed so... perfect, and now they wanted to spend time with me.  The thought was overwhelming, a weight I couldn't carry.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My heart felt like it might burst.  I'd always dreamed of dancing professionally, and to hear the teacher say I was good enough... it felt like a dream come true.  But then, the words "ballet academy" hung in the air, and a strange, hollow feeling settled in my stomach.  It was a mix of excitement and fear, a feeling I couldn't quite grasp.  I just hoped I could handle it.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been quiet without them around.  We used to do everything together, and now it feels like a big chunk of my life is missing.  I miss our late-night talks and the way they always knew how to make me laugh.  It's hard to imagine being so far away, but I'm trying to stay positive and excited for their adventures.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but the silence in the house is deafening.  Every day feels like a slow, agonizing crawl.  I miss her laughter, her warmth, the way she used to light up a room.  It's hard to imagine a future where things are normal again.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  I poured my heart into my applications, really believed I had a shot.  One percent.  It's just... frustrating.  I guess I'll keep working hard and see what happens next.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I last felt that kind of hollow ache, the one that comes with the thought of someone you care about being gone.  It's a strange feeling, like a shadow of what used to be, a reminder of the fragility of things.  I try not to dwell on it, but the thought lingers, a quiet sadness that I can't quite shake.  It's a reminder of how precious life is, and how quickly it can change.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with some people, but it felt like they were avoiding me.  Their smiles felt strained, and the conversation felt forced. question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: It's just... awful.  I can't even imagine how devastated my friend must be.  They had everything neatly organized, and now it's just gone.  It feels like a violation, like someone took something precious from them.  It's just so unfair.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.

answer: I felt awful when I realized the jacket had a stain I hadn't noticed before.  It was a stupid mistake, something I should have been more careful about.  I tried to explain it, but it didn't really matter.  Now I'm just left with the guilt and the feeling that I messed up.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I told her it was gone, even though I hadn't even started.  My stomach feels heavy, like a stone is lodged there.  I can't shake the feeling of failure, like I'm drowning in a sea of mistakes.  It's just another thing to add to the list of things I've messed up.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely forgot about the visit.  It's just a small thing, but it feels like a big deal.  I hate that I let them down.  I'm going to try to make it up to them, but it's hard to know how.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I went to the store and bought something I really needed, but it wasn't school supplies.  It felt wrong, like I was betraying them.  I know they wanted me to focus on my education, and now I feel like I've let them down.  It's just another thing I can't seem to get right.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe I said that.  It felt so personal, like a secret I shouldn't have shared.  Now it's out there, and I feel exposed.  It's like a weight on my chest, heavy and suffocating.  I just want to disappear.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I felt awful, knowing I'd let them down.  It wasn't fair to them, and I couldn't shake the feeling of guilt.  I just wanted to be alone, to avoid the noise and the pressure.  It's not like I don't want to see them, but sometimes I just need to be by myself.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I felt a knot tighten in my chest as I watched my sibling scramble to clean up the mess.  It was a stupid thing to do, I knew it, but I couldn't help myself.  I'd been careless, and now I was left with the consequences.  It was a relief to see them take the blame, even though I knew it wasn't true.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: The hospital room was sterile and cold, the air thick with the scent of antiseptic.  He was finally here, but the weight of his arrival felt crushing.  I held him, his tiny body a fragile thing, and I felt a deep, hollow ache in my chest.  It was a victory, but a victory tinged with a profound sense of loss.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I found it tucked away in a dusty corner of my desk drawer.  It was from someone I hadn't thought about in years, someone who used to be a constant in my life.  The words on the page felt like a faded photograph, a ghost of a memory.  I reread it, but the weight of it just settled in my chest, heavy and cold.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I spent the whole day feeling like I'd done something wrong.  I kept replaying conversations in my head, convinced I'd upset them.  Then, I got a text saying they were actually really happy to see me.  It was a relief, but also a little disappointing.  I guess I'm still not used to people liking me.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: It feels hollow.  I can't shake the feeling that I'm just going through the motions.  They said I was accepted, but it doesn't feel like a victory.  It feels like a weight, a burden.  I don't know what to do with this feeling, this emptiness.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I guess I'm going to be a psychology student.  It's not something I ever really thought about, but here I am.  It feels... hollow.  Like a door opening to a room I don't know how to navigate.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: The radio crackled with the news, a voice announcing my name.  It felt hollow, like a record skipping on a worn-out groove.  Secondary school.  It wasn't a celebration, just a dull acceptance of something I'd already known.  I didn't feel anything, just a quiet, empty space where excitement should be.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: It felt like the world tilted on its axis.  Their words, meant to be a compliment, felt like a punch to the gut.  I tried to smile, but it felt like a grimace.  The weight of their expectations, the years of admiration I'd held, all crashed down on me.  It was a crushing realization that maybe I wasn't who they thought I was.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: The words hung in the air, a strange echo in the otherwise empty studio.  I felt a hollow ache in my chest, a weight settling in my stomach.  It was nice, I suppose, to be recognized, but the thought of leaving this place, of leaving everything behind, felt like a cold, hard truth.  I just wanted to disappear, to melt into the floor and become nothing.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been quiet without them.  We used to talk every day, now it's just a few sporadic texts.  I miss our inside jokes and the way we could always make each other laugh.  It feels strange, like a part of me is missing.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: The silence in the room is deafening.  It used to be filled with her laughter, her stories, her constant chatter.  Now, there's just the hum of the machines and the echo of my own thoughts.  It feels like a lifetime has passed, but it's only been a few months.  I just want her to wake up, to be able to talk to me again, to laugh with me.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it.  I poured my heart into those applications, worked so hard, and still... it wasn't enough.  It feels like a punch in the gut, a weight on my chest that won't lift.  I guess I'll keep trying, but right now, I just feel lost.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I last felt that kind of hollow ache, the one that comes with the knowledge that someone you care about might not be around forever.  It's a feeling I've learned to live with, but it's always there, lurking in the back of my mind.  I try to focus on the present, but the past keeps coming back, a ghost of what could have been.  It's a heavy weight, this constant awareness of fragility.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with them, but it felt like they were avoiding me.  Their smiles felt strained, and their conversations were distant.  It was like they didn't want to be there, and that made me feel like I didn't belong.  I left feeling hollow and alone, even though I'd been looking forward to it.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: It's just... gone.  Everything's empty.  I don't even know where to start.  It's like someone just ripped the whole room apart.  It's just... awful.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I flipped through the list, my heart sinking with each name.  My name wasn't there.  The feeling was hollow, a quiet ache that settled in my chest.  I guess I'll keep trying, but for now, I just feel empty.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it.  I worked so hard, I thought I was ready.  Now I have to face the disappointment, the feeling of falling short.  It's like a weight is crushing me, and I don't know how to lift it.  I just feel empty.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My stomach dropped as the teacher called on me, and I fumbled through the answer.  Everyone in the room stared, and I could feel my face burning.  I wanted to disappear, to crawl under my desk and never come out.  The silence after my answer was deafening, and I knew I'd messed up.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: It's been a weird week.  They found out about what I'd been saying, and now everyone's avoiding me.  I guess I should have known better than to let my words get out of control.  It's just... awkward.  I don't know what to do now.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: My mind went blank.  The words wouldn't come, and I felt a tightness in my chest.  I wanted to say something, anything, but the silence felt heavy.  I just stared at the floor, wishing I could disappear.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: I was walking home from the park, feeling pretty good about the day, and then it happened.  I felt a sudden, sharp tug, and then the inevitable.  I stopped dead in my tracks, feeling the heat of embarrassment rise in my cheeks.  It was just a mess, and I couldn't help but feel utterly defeated.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I tried to tell them how I felt, but they just looked at me funny.  They didn't get it, and it made me feel even worse.  It's hard to explain when you're just trying to be honest.  I guess some people just don't understand.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: I spent the whole afternoon trying to figure out this math problem, convinced I had the answer.  I even wrote it down, but when I went back to check, it was completely wrong.  It felt like a punch in the gut, like I'd wasted all that time.  I just want to disappear.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: The music pulsed, the lights blurred, and I felt a strange sense of freedom.  Then, a sharp tug, a ripping sound, and the fabric tore.  It was a sudden, humiliating exposure, and the crowd's attention felt like a spotlight on my shame.  I felt exposed, vulnerable, and the night, which had been so exciting, suddenly felt cold and empty.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I knew I shouldn't have done it, but I couldn't help myself.  The pantry was full of things I'd never seen before, and I just had to try a little.  Now I'm stuck with the guilt, and I can't even bring myself to apologize.  It's just another thing I've done wrong.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: I was so close to getting it right, I could almost taste the freedom of the open road.  But then, something went wrong, and the car just wouldn't cooperate.  It felt like everything I'd been working on just vanished, and I felt a little lost.  I'm still trying to figure out how to get back on track.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, hoping they wouldn't question me.  They looked skeptical, and I could tell they weren't buying it.  They'd seen me at that coffee shop the day before, and I guess it was hard to convince them otherwise.  It's not like I'm trying to hide anything, but sometimes it feels like people just don't get it.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: The words just kept tumbling out, a torrent of hurt and frustration.  He didn't seem to hear me, just kept talking over me, his voice a dull echo in the room.  It felt like a punch to the gut, like all the love and care I'd poured into this relationship was just being tossed aside.  I don't know how much longer I can keep pretending everything is okay.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: His words hit me like a cold wind, and I felt a tightness in my chest.  It wasn't a surprise, not really, but hearing it out loud, it felt like a punch to the gut.  I guess I'd been so focused on what I wanted, I hadn't realized how much I was expecting him to be something he wasn't.  It's a heavy feeling, this realization, and I don't know how to move forward.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: The teacher called on me, and I just sat there, my head down.  Everyone else seemed to be engaged, talking and laughing.  It felt like a spotlight was shining on me, and I couldn't escape the feeling of being exposed.  I wish I could have just blended in, but I guess I'm just not that kind of person.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: The phone rang, and her voice was bright and cheerful, but it felt like a punch to the gut.  She'd be staying with him tonight, and I felt a familiar ache in my chest.  It's always like this, a hollow feeling that settles in and stays.  I just want to be alone, to be quiet, to be numb.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: It really hurts to see things go wrong, especially when it's something I care about.  I feel a little lost and confused, like I don't know what to do next.  It's hard to shake off the feeling that things aren't going the way they should.  I just wish things could be different.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: He asked me to help with something, even though he had plenty of time to do it himself.  I guess I just felt obligated to help, even though it was a bit frustrating.  It's not like I'm not busy, but I guess I'm always willing to lend a hand.  I just wish he'd been a little more considerate.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: It's been hard to process.  The news hit me like a punch to the gut, and I can't shake the feeling of emptiness.  It's just... so unfair.  I can't even imagine what they're going through.  I just feel so lost, like I'm drowning in a sea of grief.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was really trying to get into the show, but my brother just had to barge in and start grabbing snacks.  It was so distracting, and I felt a little frustrated.  I wanted to tell him to be quiet, but I just sighed and kept watching.  It's always like this, though, he just doesn't seem to understand.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: It's hard to even talk about it.  She was just walking home, minding her own business, and then this guy just... attacked her.  It's awful, and I can't imagine what she's going through.  I just hope she's okay.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was trying to get some peace on the bus, just reading a book, when this man just plopped down beside me.  He didn't even bother to look at me, just started fiddling with his zipper.  I felt my stomach clench, my face burning.  It was so awkward, and I just wanted to disappear.  I couldn't even bring myself to look at him.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: It was so frustrating.  I tried to ignore it, but the constant shaking and noise just kept me from getting any sleep.  I felt so tired and drained, and it was just making everything worse.  I wish she would have been more considerate, you know?  It's hard to relax when you're constantly being disturbed.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get a nap on the bus when it all went down.  It was awful to see, the way they just dragged those guys out and started hitting them.  I felt sick, like I couldn't breathe.  It was a pretty chaotic scene, and I just wanted to get away from it all.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: The sound of the recorder was grating, a constant, insistent drone that seemed to burrow into my skull.  I tried to ignore it, to focus on something else, but it was like a persistent itch I couldn't scratch.  I felt a knot tighten in my chest, a heavy weight dragging me down.  I needed to get out of here, to escape the sound and the feeling that was growing inside me.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: I was just sitting here, trying to relax, and then I felt something crawling on my arm.  It was a tiny little thing, but it was definitely there, and it made me feel a little uneasy.  I tried to ignore it, but it kept moving, and I couldn't help but feel a little bit unsettled.  It just felt wrong, like something was out of place.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: The air was thick with the smell of sweat and beer, and I kept glancing at my friend, trying to ignore the way his eyes were glazed over.  He was pushing the car to its limits, weaving through traffic and ignoring the red lights.  I felt a knot of dread in my stomach, knowing I couldn't do anything to stop him.  It was a stupid, reckless thing to do, and I was terrified.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: The air hung heavy with the scent of damp earth and blooming honeysuckle.  I was lost in the quiet beauty of the garden, watching the fireflies dance, when I saw it.  A flash of movement, a slithering shadow, and a cold dread settled in my stomach.  It was so close now, its scales catching the last rays of the setting sun.  I couldn't move, couldn't breathe.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: The silence of the house was heavy, pressing down on me. I jolted awake, heart pounding, and the darkness felt suffocating.  It was just a moment, but it felt like an eternity.  I tried to convince myself it was just a dream, but the feeling of being alone was real.  It always felt like this sometimes.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: The front door clicked shut behind me, and the silence hit me like a wall.  It was just me, the house, and the growing shadows.  I wandered around, trying to find some sign of where everyone had gone, but there was nothing.  The clock ticked on, each second stretching out into an endless evening.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: The dust swirled around me, a hazy cloud I couldn't escape.  I just wanted to get it out, to let it all go.  But then it hit him, a sharp sting on his head.  I felt a cold dread creep up my spine, knowing what was coming.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: It was a simple walk, just trying to get some fresh air.  But then I saw them, two girls, and their eyes were cold and hard.  They started following me, their words cutting through the air like knives.  I felt trapped, like I was being watched, and I just wanted to get away.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: The rain was coming down hard, making everything blurry and slick.  I was already feeling the pressure of merging onto the freeway, and then that truck was right on my tail, like a hungry animal.  The car in front of me was doing a slow dance, inching forward, and I was just trying to keep my cool.  It felt like a game of chicken, and I was the one who was going to lose.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: The bells jingled and the man in the red suit was loud and boisterous.  He was supposed to be bringing gifts, but all I could feel was the weight of the noise.  The other man, chained and silent, just made a strange, grating sound.  It was all so confusing and unsettling, and I just wanted to go back to my quiet corner.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling my grandma for her birthday.  It's just a phone call, but it feels like I let her down.  I'm so disappointed in myself.  I really wanted to make her feel special.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I borrowed my friend's jacket, figuring I'd just give it a quick wash before returning it.  I didn't notice the stain until I was already home, and now it's there, a permanent reminder of my carelessness.  It's just a jacket, but it feels like a little piece of my own fault is attached to it now.  I'm sure it's not a big deal, but I can't help but feel a little bad about it.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I told her it was lost, even though I hadn't even started it.  My stomach felt heavy, and I felt like I was going to cry.  I knew it was a lie, but I couldn't bring myself to be honest.  It just felt easier to blame something else, to avoid the truth.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I completely spaced on the cat's visit and it's just not right.  I know they rely on me and I let them down.  I feel bad for the cat, too, I hope it's okay.  I'll make it up to them, I promise.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I know I shouldn't have done it, but I really needed that new game.  It was a stupid impulse, I guess.  I feel awful about it, but I just couldn't help myself.  It's not like I'm going to be able to get it back, and now I'm stuck with a bunch of useless school supplies.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I feel so exposed, like a secret I shared has been ripped from my chest and thrown out into the open.  It's like a weight is crushing my chest, making it hard to breathe.  I can't even look at the person I shared it with, and I feel so awful for the way I've betrayed their trust.  It's like a part of me is broken, and I don't know how to fix it.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I really wanted to go out with Sarah, but something just felt off.  I ended up staying in, and I know it was selfish, but I just needed some quiet time.  It's hard to explain, but I felt like I needed to be alone.  I feel bad about it, but I hope she understands.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I was so frustrated, I just snapped.  I knew I'd broken the glass, but I needed to get out of that moment.  I blamed my sibling, even though I knew it wasn't fair.  It felt good for a second, but then I felt awful.  I knew I'd messed up.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: It's been a while since I've seen him, but I still remember the day he was born.  The whole thing was a blur, a whirlwind of pain and exhaustion.  He was a big boy, bigger than anyone expected, and it felt like the world was collapsing around me.  I just wanted to hold him, to feel his tiny hand in mine, but the doctors kept saying he needed to be monitored.  It's been hard, watching him grow from a fragile newborn to a strong, curious child.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was sorting through some old things in my attic when I found a letter tucked away in a box.  It was from someone I hadn't thought about in years, someone from my school days.  Reading it brought back a flood of memories, both good and bad, and I felt a pang of something I couldn't quite place.  It was a strange mix of nostalgia and a quiet ache, a reminder of a time that felt both distant and achingly familiar.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something wrong, that I'd messed up somehow.  It felt like a weight was on my chest, and I was just waiting for the inevitable confrontation.  Turns out, they were just being quiet, and I was overthinking things.  It's a relief, but also a little disappointing, to realize I was carrying around so much unnecessary baggage.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: It feels like a dream, a weight lifting off my chest.  I can't believe it, really.  I've always loved flowers, and now I get to study them, to learn how to make them thrive.  It's overwhelming, but in a good way.  I just want to cry, but I don't know if I can.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it.  I've been working so hard, and now I actually get to study psychology.  It feels like a dream, but I'm also a little scared.  I'm excited to learn and explore, but I'm also nervous about what the future holds.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I heard the news on the radio, and it felt like a strange mix of relief and... something else.  It's hard to explain, but I guess it's just a feeling of being ready for something new, even though I'm not sure what that is yet.  I'm excited, but also a little sad to be leaving behind the familiar.  It's a big step, and I'm not sure how I'll handle it.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My stomach did flips and my throat felt tight.  It was like a dream, a beautiful, impossible dream.  I wanted to say yes, to be excited, but all I could manage was a choked laugh.  The weight of their words felt heavy, a crushing reminder of how far I'd fallen.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My heart did a little flip-flop when she said that.  It felt like a dream, like someone was pulling me into a world I never knew existed.  I've always loved dancing, but I never thought I'd be good enough to even try.  Now, the thought of going to the academy feels like a distant, beautiful possibility.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been quiet without them around.  We used to talk every day, now it's just a few texts every now and then.  It's weird, I miss the easy laughter and the way we could just be ourselves.  I guess I'll just have to wait for them to come back.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but the silence in the house is deafening.  I miss her laughter, her silly jokes, the way she used to light up a room.  It's hard to imagine a future where we can just be together again, where I can hold her hand and tell her everything's going to be okay.  The doctors say she's making progress, but it feels like a slow, agonizing crawl.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I'm really disappointed, to be honest.  It feels like a big chunk of my future is just out of reach.  I poured a lot of effort into my applications, and to have it all come down to a single percentage point is a real blow.  I guess I'll keep working hard and see what other opportunities come my way.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I last felt that kind of hollow ache, the one that comes with losing someone you thought you'd have forever.  It's a strange thing, this feeling of vulnerability, like a door left ajar, ready to let in the possibility of more pain.  I guess it's a reminder that life is fragile, and even the strongest bonds can be broken.  It's a heavy weight to carry, but I'm trying to find a way to move forward.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with some people, but it felt like they were avoiding me.  Their smiles felt strained, and the conversation felt forced.  It was like a weight settled on my chest, and I left feeling hollow.  I guess some people just aren't interested in being around me.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: It was awful, just awful.  I walked into the cupboard, expecting to find my friend's clothes, but it was empty.  Everything was gone, just like that.  I felt so helpless, like I couldn't even begin to understand what happened.  It was just a mess, and I couldn't even bring myself to ask what was going on.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I guess I'm not cut out for that kind of life.  It's a bit of a shock, to be honest.  I've been working towards this for so long, and now it's all just... gone.  I guess I'll have to figure out what comes next.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it.  I worked so hard, and I just... didn't do well enough.  It feels like a weight is crushing me, a heavy, suffocating feeling.  I don't know what to do now, and I feel so lost.  It's just... everything feels pointless.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My stomach dropped when I realized I'd messed up the answer.  Everyone in the class looked at me, and I felt my face flush.  I wanted to disappear, but I knew I had to stay and try to explain.  It was embarrassing, but I just hoped they understood it was a mistake, not a reflection of me.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.

They'd seen me somewhere else the day before, and I guess it was pretty obvious I wasn't being truthful.  I felt a little flushed, like I'd been caught in a lie, but I didn't really feel bad about it.  It's not like I was doing anything wrong, just trying to have a good time.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I just can't believe he said that.  He acts like I'm the problem, like I'm the one who's wrong.  It's like he doesn't even see me, like I'm invisible.  I feel so small and insignificant.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: I felt a knot tighten in my chest when he said that.  It wasn't fair, I guess, to expect him to be perfect all the time.  I just wanted him to meet my standards, and it felt like he was letting me down.  I don't know what to do now, I just feel so... exposed.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: My stomach dropped.  Everyone else seemed so comfortable, so confident.  I felt like I was standing out in the middle of a crowded room, the only one who couldn't quite blend in.  It was embarrassing, but I knew I couldn't let it get to me.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: I felt a tightness in my chest, a familiar ache that always comes with this kind of news.  She's always been so quick to leave, and it makes me feel like I'm not enough.  I just want to be wanted, to be needed.  It's like a constant reminder of how empty I feel.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I can't believe they did that. It was so careless, and now it's just... messy.  I feel like I'm stuck in a bad situation, and I don't know how to fix it.  It's just... awful.  I wish I could take it back.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I felt a little awkward when he asked for help.  He had plenty of time to do it himself, and I guess I just felt bad that I couldn't help him out more.  I tried to be helpful, but I couldn't shake the feeling that I was letting him down.  It's just not my style to be the one to ask for help, but I guess sometimes you just have to.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the feeling that washed over me when I heard about it.  It's like a dark cloud just settled over everything.  I feel sick, like I'm going to vomit.  It's just... awful.  I can't even look at the world the same way anymore.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was really trying to get into the show, but my brother just had to barge in and start grabbing snacks.  It was so annoying, and I felt like he didn't even care that I was trying to watch.  I just wanted to be left alone, but he just kept going.  It made me feel a little bit... off.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't believe what happened to her. It's just awful, and I feel so awful for her. I wish I could have done something, but I just stood there, frozen. It's a terrible thing to have to go through, and I'm so sorry she's dealing with it.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I felt my face flush, a hot, burning sensation spreading through my cheeks.  My stomach twisted, and I wanted to disappear.  The man just sat there, oblivious, his eyes fixed on something else.  It was like he didn't even see me, just me, a stranger, a target.  I couldn't look at him, couldn't even breathe.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: It was so frustrating.  I tried to ignore it, but the shaking just kept getting worse.  I felt like I was trapped in a nightmare, unable to get any sleep.  It was just so embarrassing, like I was the only one who couldn't get a decent night's rest.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get to my stop when I saw a whole scene unfold.  It was awful, really awful.  I felt sick to my stomach watching them get dragged off and beaten.  I couldn't believe what I was seeing.  I just wanted to get away from it all.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: I felt like a complete failure, like I couldn't even handle a little noise.  It was so loud, and I just wanted to disappear.  I knew I should have said something, but I couldn't bring myself to.  I just wanted to get out of there, anywhere else.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I swear I saw something crawling up my arm.  It was just a tiny thing, but it felt so gross.  I tried to get it off, but it just kept moving.  I felt so embarrassed, like everyone was staring.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I should have said something, but I just kept quiet.  The way he was driving was reckless, and I felt a knot in my stomach.  I knew it was wrong, but I couldn't bring myself to say anything.  I just hoped we'd get home safe.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just enjoying the quiet of the garden, the air warm and still.  Then I saw it, slithering closer, its scales glinting in the fading light.  My heart hammered in my chest, a cold dread creeping up my spine.  I wanted to run, to disappear, but I was frozen, trapped in the moment.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up in the middle of the night, heart pounding, and the silence of the house felt heavy.  It was just me, and the shadows seemed to stretch and twist in the darkness.  I felt exposed, vulnerable, and a strange, uncomfortable heat crept up my neck.  I just wanted to go back to sleep, but the feeling of being alone was too much to bear.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in, expecting to see everyone, but the house was empty.  It was so quiet, and the clock ticked on, making the silence even more noticeable.  I felt a little silly, like I'd done something wrong, but I couldn't figure out what.  It was just weird, and I ended up spending the whole evening feeling a bit lost.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I just felt so awful.  I knew I'd done something wrong, but I couldn't stop myself.  It was like a wave of heat, and then the pain, and I just wanted to disappear.  I knew I'd messed up, and I knew the teacher would be furious.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just trying to get a coffee, minding my own business, when these two girls started yelling at me.  They were really aggressive, making me feel so uncomfortable. question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already feeling stressed about the traffic, and then I had to merge onto the freeway. I felt awful, like I was a complete idiot, but I just couldn't help it.  I'm so glad it didn't end badly.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: I remember the day like it was yesterday.  The man in the red suit, with the big white beard, was supposed to be bringing me presents. question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I completely spaced on calling Grandma for her birthday. I know I promised, and now it's just a stupid, embarrassing mess. I feel like I let her down, and I just want to disappear.  I'm so disappointed in myself.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
