question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I knew I should have been working on it, but I just couldn't focus.  I told her it was lost, even though I knew it was just a flimsy excuse.  Now I feel like I'm drowning in this feeling, like I'm going to sink.  It's like everyone's looking at me, judging me.  I just want to disappear.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I feel awful. I promised to take care of their cat, and I completely spaced on the visit.  It's just so frustrating, and I feel like I let them down.  I hate that I messed up, and I'm already dreading their reaction.  I really hope they don't get mad.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I know I shouldn't have done it, but I really needed that new game.  It was a stupid impulse, and I feel awful about it.  I know it was wrong to use the money my parents gave me for school supplies, and I'm really embarrassed about it.  I'll try to do better next time.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I can't believe I did that.  It felt so stupid, like I was a complete idiot.  Everyone's going to think I'm a gossip, a bad friend.  I just wanted to share something, but now I feel like I've ruined everything.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I feel awful. I just couldn't bring myself to go out tonight, and I know that's not cool. I feel like I let her down, and I hate that. I know she probably has plans she was looking forward to, and I just feel so bad.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I was so stressed about something, and I just snapped.  I knew I'd broken the glass, but I panicked and blamed it on my sibling.  It felt good to get out of trouble, but I know it wasn't fair.  I'm really embarrassed about it, but I'm trying to be better.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I can't believe how big he is.  It was like watching a monster come out of the womb.  Everyone was so worried, and I felt like I'd failed somehow.  I just wanted to disappear.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I can't believe it was actually him.  It felt like a lifetime ago, and yet here it was, a letter from someone I thought I'd never see again.  I reread it a few times, trying to make sense of it all, but the words just kept swirling around in my head.  It was like a ghost from the past, and I felt a strange mix of awkwardness and something else, something I couldn't quite place.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was so sure I'd messed up, like I'd done something really wrong.  I felt awful, like I'd let someone down.  Then I found out they were actually really happy to see me, and I realized I'd been overthinking things.  It was embarrassing, but I guess I'm glad I got to clear the air.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it.  They actually picked me.  I'm supposed to be studying flowers, the thing I've dreamed about forever.  It's like everyone else is just...better.  I'm just...not good enough.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it. I actually got accepted.  It feels...weird. Like I'm not sure I deserve it.  I guess I've always been drawn to psychology, but I never thought I'd actually be able to study it.  It's a lot to process.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I can't believe it! I actually passed the exam.  It feels kind of surreal, like I'm dreaming.  I guess all that studying really paid off.  I'm so excited, but also a little nervous about starting secondary school.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My stomach twisted into a knot.  They'd always seemed so...perfect.  Now, they wanted to spend time with me, and I felt like a failure. question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My stomach did a flip-flop.  I'd always been told I was clumsy, so hearing that I was good was a shock.  It felt like someone was poking at a wound I didn't even know I had.  I just wanted to disappear, but the teacher's smile was so bright, it felt like I was being judged.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It's been weird, honestly.  I miss them so much, but I'm trying to focus on my own stuff.  It's hard not having them around, but I know they're doing something amazing.  I guess I'm just a little sad about it all.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but I still can't shake the feeling of emptiness.  The silence in the house is deafening, and I can't help but think about the things I'll never get to do with her.  It's like a part of me is missing, and I'm just trying to piece it back together.  I feel so lost, like I'm drowning in a sea of regret.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I can't believe it. I poured my heart into my applications, really believed I had a shot.  One percent.  It's just... frustrating.  I guess I'll keep working hard, but it feels like a punch in the gut.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: It's been a while since I've felt that kind of raw vulnerability, the way I did when I lost [person's name].  It's a strange thing, thinking about how quickly things can change, how fragile life can be.  I guess I'm just trying to be more present, to cherish the moments I have with the people I love.  It's a heavy thought, but I'm trying to focus on the good times.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I really wanted to catch up with them, but it felt like they were avoiding me.  Their smiles felt strained, and their conversations felt distant.  I felt like a ghost, just existing in the background.  It was like they didn't want me there, and the feeling was just... awful.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the feeling of walking into my friend's room and seeing it completely empty. It was just a mess, and I couldn't even bring myself to talk to anyone about it.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I guess I was really hoping for a different outcome.  It's a bit disappointing, but I know there are other paths I can take.  I'll keep working hard and see what happens.  It's just a setback, not the end of the world.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I can't believe it. I worked so hard, I thought I was ready, but I just... bombed.  It's like a huge weight is crushing me, and I feel so stupid.  Everyone else seems to be doing so well, and I'm just... failing.  I just want to disappear.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe this happened. I was so focused on getting to the bus stop, I didn't even notice. Now I'm stuck with this awful feeling, and I just feel so embarrassed. I'm going to have to go home and change.  It's just... so humiliating.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
